camps.name: Pinal County Fairgrounds & Event Center campground
camps.access: Paved and flat, but backwards: from downtown Casa Grande (mile 0) ride about 11.5 mi EAST via E Florence Blvd toward Eleven Mile Corner, then to 512 S Eleven Mile Corner Rd.
camps.address: 512 S Eleven Mile Corner Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85194
camps.priceTent: $10 cash ($10.43 card) per tent per night for dry/tent camping with restrooms and showers; $25 cash ($25.85 card) for a site with water and 30/50A electric if you want power; weekly rates available.
camps.reservations: No reservations; first-come, first-served. After hours, pay at the box by the office or find the camp host on duty (reviewers say call before closing so the host can let you in). 14-night limit per 6 months; checkout 11 am. Blackouts: Oct 30-Nov 1 2026 dry camping only (motorcycle swap meet); NO open camping Nov 16-19 2026. Nov 2-15 is normal.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the only tent-legal campground in the Casa Grande area. Every in-town park is 55+ and/or RV-only (see gapWarnings). It is 11.5 mi behind you if you're heading west, so it only makes sense for a rest day. Open lot with no designated tent pads. Animals and noise during events. No fires on pavement, no firearms.

camps.name: Casa Grande RV Resort & Cottages
camps.access: Paved, about 3 mi north of downtown on N Pinal Ave at W Rodeo Rd.
camps.address: 195 W Rodeo Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85122
camps.priceTent: No tent sites. RV sites were about $77/night (reported Mar 2025); cottages are lodging, not camping.
camps.reservations: Office open Mon-Sat 9 am-4 pm, closed Sunday.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the trip app's 'Unnamed campground' (OSM way 1348098748) at Pinal Ave & Rodeo Rd. AAA lists it as 'No tent - RVs only', and the operator advertises only 282 RV sites and 34 cottages. All ages, but not a tent option.

camps.name: RoVer's Roost RV Retreat (Escapees SKP Co-op)
camps.access: Paved; southwest of Casa Grande at 3241 S Montgomery Rd.
camps.address: 3241 S Montgomery Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85193
camps.priceTent: Not applicable: a 55+ RV co-op, and no tent sites are offered.
camps.reservations: RV stays and Escapees co-op membership only.
camps.cyclistNotes: Self-described '55+ Escapees Co-Op' for RVers, so not a tent option. The adjacent unnamed OSM 'campground' polygon on W Selma Hwy (way 761144406) sits beside it and is not a tent option either.

camps.name: Silverado RV Resort (Eloy)
camps.access: Paved, about 11 mi southeast of Casa Grande in Eloy (Tonto Rd / La Brea St), behind you.
camps.priceTent: Not applicable: a 55+ RV resort.
camps.reservations: unknown
camps.cyclistNotes: Listed by Campendium as 'Silverado 55+ RV Resort'. This is a baseline app entry that should be marked not usable for a tent camper.

camps.name: Wild West RV Ranch (primitive tent site)
camps.access: Paved state highways, flat. From Maricopa (mile 21.7) ride about 12.5 mi south on AZ 347 / John Wayne Pkwy to AZ 84 ('Peters Corner'). Alternative: from Casa Grande ride about 18 mi west on AZ 84 through Stanfield to the ranch, then about 12.5 mi north on AZ 347 to Maricopa next morning. That adds about 9 mi to the planned line.
camps.address: 860 S John Wayne Pkwy (AZ 347 at AZ 84, Peters Corner), Maricopa, AZ 85139
camps.priceTent: Primitive tent site booked via Hipcamp. The listing shows 'from $25/night'; one directory quoted the tent site at $40. Includes restrooms, hot showers, a water spigot, Wi-Fi, a picnic table and a fire pit. The tent site has no electric; RV sites have 30/50A pedestals (RV from about $50, Good Sam).
camps.reservations: Book on Hipcamp; same-day bookings accepted. Check-in from 2 pm with a host meet-and-greet; call for a late arrival. Open all year, all ages.
camps.cyclistNotes: The best real tent campground between Casa Grande and Buckeye: a dedicated primitive tent site near restrooms and hot showers. Tent campers reviewed it in Aug and Oct 2026 (clean bathroom, easy check-in, some shade). Its own websites are dead (wildwestrvranch.com is an unconnected Wix domain; the old wildwestrvresort.com is now spam), so use Hipcamp or the phone. Main drawback: 12.5 mi off the line each way.

camps.name: Harrah's Ak-Chin Casino overnight RV lot (emergency only)
camps.access: Paved: from the line in Maricopa ride about 2.5 mi south on AZ 347 / John Wayne Pkwy.
camps.priceTent: Free. Overnight RV/vehicle parking only, per reviewers; tent use is not documented anywhere.
camps.reservations: Ask security or the front desk before setting up. In 2022 security first turned an RVer away, then allowed the back lot. No stated night limit.
camps.cyclistNotes: Last-resort fallback on Ak-Chin tribal land. The documented use is RVs sleeping in a parking lot, not tents, and the casino's own site says nothing about RV parking, so ask and accept a 'no'. 24-hour restrooms, food and water inside. Semis also use the lot at night. The newest reviews are from 2022.

camps.name: BLM dispersed: desert tracks between AZ 238 and Empire Blvd (south end of Sierra Estrella)
camps.access: On the line itself. From about mile 31.3 (N Rahma St off AZ 238) the route leaves pavement and follows unnamed OSM tracks across BLM land north to 'Empire Blvd'. Surface is dirt and sand with wash crossings; BLM calls these roads 'extremely sandy or silty' and requires 4WD to reach the wilderness boundary. Per BLM's land-status GIS, the line is on BLM land for most of miles 31-42.
camps.address: BLM public land along the route's dirt tracks north of AZ 238 near N Rahma St, Maricopa County
camps.priceTent: Free; no permit. BLM limit is 14 days in any 28-day period.
camps.reservations: None; first come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Free, legal, no facilities at all. At miles 39-42 camp WEST of the north-south track: the Sierra Estrella Wilderness boundary is just east, and bikes are banned inside (the line passes about 165 ft from it at mile 42). A mapped BLM vault toilet sits at the Quartz Peak trailhead, about 1.7 mi east of mile 41.7, but the way there is deep sand. Tribal land is only 0.3-1 mi away near miles 28-34, so don't stray onto it. Carry all water from Maricopa; nothing is available from mile 25 to 58. Rainbow Valley BLM land gets target shooters, so camp out of sight of the track. Fireworks and exploding targets are banned year-round; seasonal fire restrictions were lifted July 22, 2026. No Lower Sonoran camping closures or BLM Arizona alerts were listed on Nov 1, 2026.

camps.name: BLM dispersed: unpaved W Riggs Rd section (miles 45-47)
camps.access: On the line: the unpaved track / 'W Riggs Rd' section between Empire Blvd and the start of pavement at about mile 48.6 crosses BLM land at about miles 45-47. Dirt and sand.
camps.address: BLM land along W Riggs Rd (unpaved) east of S 163rd Ave, Rainbow Valley, Maricopa County
camps.priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: The last free camp right on the line before pavement resumes. Rainbow Valley homes start just west; only the BLM block is legal, so stay clear of private parcels. No water; the nearest is a fire station about 12 mi ahead (mile 57.8).

camps.name: BLM dispersed: west end of W Riggs Rd past Rainbow Valley Rd
camps.access: At the W Riggs Rd / S Rainbow Valley Rd junction (mile 52.6, where the line turns north), keep going WEST about 1.1-1.2 mi on W Riggs Rd (gravel per OSM) to BLM land at the north end of the Maricopa Mountains. S 189th Ave / Baseline Rd (unpaved) and a track about 1 mi south of the junction also reach BLM land.
camps.address: End of W Riggs Rd west of S Rainbow Valley Rd, Rainbow Valley, Maricopa County
camps.priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: The closest legal free camp to paved Rainbow Valley Rd, about mile 50-53, which fits a 50-mile wind day. Residential lots border the BLM land, so camp well inside the boundary. Nearest water: Goodyear Fire Station 6, about 5 mi on at mile 57.8 (ask).

camps.name: BLM dispersed: W Ray Rd west of S Tuthill Rd (Buckeye Hills east)
camps.access: Where the line turns from W Ray Rd north onto S Tuthill Rd (about mile 61), continue about 0.9-1.3 mi west on W Ray Rd (asphalt per OSM) to BLM land.
camps.address: W Ray Rd west of S Tuthill Rd, south of Buckeye, Maricopa County
camps.priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Land status comes only from BLM GIS; no camper reports found. The point is not inside the Lower Gila Terraces ACEC (checked against BLM's ACEC layer). Equestrian and other private parcels are nearby, so obey any 'no trespassing' signs. Fire Station 326 is right on the line at mile 61.2 for water.

camps.name: Estrella Mountain Regional Park new campground (under construction)
camps.access: Paved Goodyear arterials: from S Tuthill Rd at about mile 62.5, ride about 8-9 mi east (Elliot Rd / Estrella Pkwy / Vineyard Ave) to the park entrance at 14805 W Vineyard Ave.
camps.priceTent: unknown; rates for the new campground not found.
camps.reservations: Maricopa County Parks online system (exploremaricopacountyparks.org / reservations.maricopacounty.gov), up to 6 months ahead. The county says the park only 'periodically' rents host sites; call.
camps.cyclistNotes: Don't count on it. The county says the 50-site campground (2 restroom buildings with showers, dump station) is under construction Feb 2025 through Mar 2027. Jan 2026 commission minutes said work continues, and an Apr 29, 2026 county release still called it 'under development'. If it has opened early, it would be the only shower campground between Maricopa and Buckeye. Phone before detouring.

camps.name: Vescent RV Park
camps.access: Paved, about 1 mi north of the line on Buckeye's east side, on MC 85 next to Vescent Church.
camps.priceTent: unknown
camps.reservations: unknown
camps.cyclistNotes: Appears only in OpenStreetMap; no website, phone or reviews found. It shares its location with Vescent Church. Worth asking in person while passing through Buckeye, but treat it as unverified.

camps.name: The Sunset Nooks (Hipcamp)
camps.access: Paved city streets on the south side of Buckeye, about 1 mi off Beloat Rd. Hipcamp gives the exact address after booking (the map pin is approximate). Walk in from parking.
camps.address: South Buckeye, AZ 85326 (exact address after booking)
camps.priceTent: Hipcamp listing from $55/night for one tent-only site ('Mendo', up to 8 people). Includes portable toilets, potable water, Wi-Fi, a cold shower when the host is on site, and the host's easy-up canopy and grill gear.
camps.reservations: Hipcamp; same-day bookings welcome. Check-in after 2 pm; music off at 10 pm.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only tent-specific site found in Buckeye, about 1 mi off the line. A small private property a 2-minute walk from a lake; host Cory got strong reviews from tent campers in Mar, Apr and Oct 2026. It is a single site, so book before rolling in. Toilets are portable units, and the shower is cold and only available when the host is there.

camps.name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
camps.access: Paved: from Beloat Rd ride about 8 mi straight north on Watson Rd (crossing I-10 at exit 117) to 2600 N Watson Rd. The last 2 mi climb about 500-600 ft into the White Tank foothills (camp elevation 1,476 ft).
camps.priceTent: $20/night per site (last reported Dec 2025). Restrooms with sinks and toilets; no water, showers or hookups.
camps.reservations: 7 primitive sites (A-G). Reserve online through the City of Buckeye at least 3 days ahead; unreserved walk-up stays are limited to one night (Dec 2025 review). Max 7 nights. The gate reportedly locks around 10 pm (one report says 9:30 pm), so arrive early.
camps.cyclistNotes: Legal, cheap, quiet and dark, but completely dry: the city says there is no drinking water in the park. Fill up in Buckeye (Circle K on Monroe Ave) before the climb. Sites C-E are farther from the busy trailhead. It is a 17-mi round-trip detour north, not on the way west.

camps.name: Leaf Verde RV Resort (Sun Outdoors / Sun RV)
camps.access: Paved, about 4.5 mi north of downtown Buckeye on Apache Rd, near I-10.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites listed. RV sites were about $85/night (May 2024).
camps.reservations: Office reportedly closed on weekends (2024).
camps.cyclistNotes: A large Sun Communities RV park with mostly long-term residents. Its Hipcamp property listing shows only RV site types (Standard/Deluxe/Premium, 376 sites) and reviewers call the Wi-Fi unusable. Expect 'RVs only'. Note that leafverde.com now redirects to Sun Outdoors.

camps.name: BLM dispersed off W Robbins Butte Game Rd (south of Buckeye; 'Buckeye Hills BLM')
camps.access: From the line at Buckeye, take AZ 85 south across the Gila River (about 4-5 mi on the highway shoulder) to W Robbins Butte Game Rd, then 1-2 mi west on dirt with soft gravel and sand spots. Campers use a strip of about 1 mi on the SOUTH side of the road.
camps.address: W Robbins Butte Game Rd off AZ 85, Buckeye, AZ
camps.priceTent: Free
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Last resort only. Legality is muddled: 'no overnight camping / no shooting' signs were seen in Apr 2025, rangers told campers 'no camping' in 2021, the adjoining Robbins Butte Wildlife Area (AZ Game & Fish) bans camping, and The Dyrt lists the nearby 'Buckeye Hills BLM' spot as CLOSED. People were still camping there in Jan-Feb 2026, and a sheriff patrols mornings. Reviews from 2021-2026 report heavy shooting (ricochets near a trailer in Aug 2024), theft, dumping and crowding. Not a good place for a solo tent.

research.waterAndFood:
Casa Grande (mile 0) has everything. Miles 2-19 run through farm country on the Casa Grande-Maricopa Hwy, with nothing mapped within about 1.5 mi of the line (about 17 mi).

Maricopa (miles 19-23) is the LAST real resupply:
- On the line at mile 19: Walmart Supercenter, Big 5 Sporting Goods (stove fuel), Walgreens.
- On the line at mile 21.6: Chevron with a c-store, Dairy Queen.
- Within 1 mi of miles 21.7-22.6: Fry's Marketplace, Bashas', Sprouts, QuikTrip, Circle K.
- Mile 23.1: Maricopa Fire Station 575, on the line.
- Last food: Arroyo Grille restaurant/bar, mile 25.1, 0.3 mi off.

After that there is NOTHING through the dirt section until:
- Goodyear Fire Station 6 (18430 W Willis Rd), mile 57.8, 0.3 mi off. Ask for water.
- Tempo Café at the CantaMia Village Center, mile 57.5, about 1 mi off. It is a 55+ community clubhouse and public access is uncertain.
- Arizona Fire Medical Authority Station 326, mile 61.2, on the line.
- South Lake Park restrooms in Estrella, about 2.3 mi off at mile 61.

The first store after Maricopa is in Buckeye (miles 69-71): Circle K and Chevron on Monroe Ave, Subway, Piñata Market, restaurants, and the Earl Edgar Park restrooms.

Longest stretches:
- No store: about 47 mi (QuikTrip in Maricopa at about mile 22.5 to Circle K in Buckeye at about 69.9).
- No water source of any kind: about 33 mi (mile 25 to the Goodyear fire station at 57.8), or about 36 mi to the on-line fire station at 61.2.

Leave Maricopa with at least 5-6 L. Take 8 L or more if you plan to sleep on the BLM dirt section: that covers dinner, breakfast and 10-25 sandy miles before the first tap. There is no water at any BLM site, at Skyline Regional Park, or at Robbins Butte.
research.legality:
There is no interstate in this segment; every road is legal for bikes.

Miles 0 to about 31 are paved: W Main Ave → Casa Grande-Maricopa Hwy / W Maricopa-Casa Grande Hwy → Cowtown Rd → Maricopa streets → AZ 238 (Maricopa Rd) west. I could not confirm shoulder widths.

ROAD WARNING: from about mile 31.3 (N Rahma St, OSM surface 'ground') to about mile 48.6, the planned line follows about 17 miles of UNPAVED track across BLM desert: unnamed OSM tracks, 'Empire Blvd' (a track) and the dirt part of W Riggs Rd. Pavement resumes on W Riggs Rd at mile 48.6.
- BLM's Sierra Estrella Wilderness page says the dirt roads on this side are 'extremely sandy or silty' with deep wash crossings, and 4WD is needed to reach the wilderness boundary.
- A Dec 2025 review of the Quartz Peak approach (same area) reports about 12 mi of deep sand where a vehicle turned back.
- Expect to push a loaded bike through stretches. Don't attempt it after rain. There are no services and almost no traffic.
- The track passes about 165 ft from the Sierra Estrella Wilderness boundary at mile 42. Bicycles are banned inside the wilderness, so stay on the track.
- Tribal land lies 0.3-1 mi from the line at miles 28-34. Don't camp or ride off-route there.

Miles 48.6-71 are paved (W Riggs Rd, S Rainbow Valley Rd, W Willis Rd / W Ray Rd, S Tuthill Rd, Beloat Rd, Buckeye streets), apart from short unpaved connectors at about miles 60.5-61.5, 64.4-64.7 and 67.4.

Paved alternative (not checked in detail): stay on AZ 238 west through Mobile to Gila Bend, then take AZ 85 north to Buckeye. It is roughly 25-30 mi longer, but has BLM camping along AZ 238 (Sonoran Desert National Monument) and full services in Gila Bend.

BLM Arizona rules: dispersed camping is allowed for 14 days in any 28. Fireworks, exploding targets and tracer rounds are banned year-round. Seasonal fire restrictions were lifted July 22, 2026. No BLM Arizona alerts or Lower Sonoran camping closures were listed on Nov 1, 2026.
research.gapWarnings:
Tent-legal options by line mile (Casa Grande = 0):
- Mile 0: Pinal County Fairgrounds, 11.5 mi EAST, i.e. backwards.
- Mile 14: Wild West RV Ranch, about 12.5 mi off via AZ 347 or AZ 84.
- Mile 20: Harrah's Ak-Chin RV lot. Tent use is not documented.
- Miles 31-42 and 45-47: free BLM land right on the line, on the dirt section.
- Mile 52.6: BLM land 1.2 mi off at the end of W Riggs Rd.
- Mile 61: BLM land about 1 mi off on W Ray Rd (low confidence).
- Mile 62.5: Estrella Mountain Regional Park, about 9 mi off. Probably still under construction.
- Miles 68-70 (Buckeye): The Sunset Nooks Hipcamp about 1 mi off; Skyline Regional Park 8.5 mi off; Vescent RV Park unverified.
- Mile 73: Robbins Butte BLM, about 6.5 mi off. Questionable legality and safety.

1) Miles 0 to about 31: no tent-legal spot within 10 mi of the line. Casa Grande itself has none. Every in-town park is 55+ and/or RV-only: Casa Grande RV Resort, Palm Creek, Fiesta Grande, Sundance 1, Leisure Valley, Foothills West, Casita Verde, Val Vista, Sunscape, RoVer's Roost and Silverado. Fallbacks:
   - Wild West RV Ranch (tent site with hot showers). Either ride Casa Grande → AZ 84 → ranch, about 18 mi, or go 12.5 mi south from Maricopa.
   - Pinal County Fairgrounds ($10, showers, behind you).
   - Ask Harrah's Ak-Chin security.

2) No campground with showers or water from Wild West (mile 14, 12.5 mi off) to Buckeye's Sunset Nooks (about mile 70, cold shower only when the host is there). That is about 56 line-miles. Estrella's new shower campground would fill the gap only if it has opened, which I could not confirm.

3) If the 17 dirt miles (31-48) are unrideable and you reroute on pavement via AZ 238 → Gila Bend → AZ 85, you lose the BLM sites on the line. Use BLM land along AZ 238 instead, such as Margies Cove West in the Sonoran Desert National Monument: 3 sites, vault toilet, no water, about 5 mi of dirt east of AZ 85 at Woods Rd (about milepost 134).

Last-resort legal option: Arizona State Trust Land lies within about 0.5 mi of the line at many points (miles 8-24 and 52-62). Camping there needs an ASLD recreational permit, about $15/yr for an individual and bought online, with camping capped at roughly 14 days a year. Stay off leased farm fields and posted parcels. I could not open ASLD's site (Cloudflare block) to reconfirm the 2026 terms.

Excluded or not usable:
- Buckeye Hills Regional Park: primitive camping ended Jan 21, 2018.
- Robbins Butte Wildlife Area: no camping.
- Unnamed OSM 'caravan_site' areas at S Hasienda Rd near Arizona City (32.7614,-111.6492) and W Hazen Rd in Buckeye (33.3528,-112.5981): no evidence of overnight or tent use.
- The baseline's 'Unnamed campground' on N Pinal Ave is Casa Grande RV Resort (RVs only). The one on W Selma Hwy adjoins RoVer's Roost (55+).
- Parkside Trailer Court, Buckeye: residential trailer court.
- Destiny RV Resort (Goodyear): its website now shows a resort in Blythe, so its status is unclear.
- Cotton Lane RV Resort (Goodyear): 55+. Both Goodyear parks are about 7-8 mi north of mile 64.

Research note: the shared web-search quota ran out partway through. Later checks used direct page fetches, OpenStreetMap and Nominatim, and BLM land-status GIS. I could not see Skyline Regional Park's official page (blocked); its fee and reservation rules come from Campendium reviews.

camps.name: The Sunset Nooks (Hipcamp tent site)
camps.access: Small private lot in south Buckeye by the Gila River, about 1 mile off the line at the Buckeye end (street address shown after booking). Paved streets, walk-in tent pad.
camps.priceTent: $55/night for the single tent site (about $64.53 all-in with the Hipcamp fee), up to 8 people. Host supplies a pop-up tent, table, chairs, BBQ and charcoal.
camps.phone: unknown (contact host Cory W. through the Hipcamp app)
camps.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice needed. Message the host with your ETA. Music down at 8pm, off at 10pm.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the only bookable tent pitch with a shower and toilet at the Buckeye end: 44 bookings, 96% recommend. It sits at corridor mile ~70, the start of this segment, so it works as a Buckeye night, not a mid-segment stop. A toilet is listed but its type isn't stated.

camps.name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
camps.access: 2600 N Watson Rd, Buckeye. About 9 miles north of the line on paved Watson Rd (crosses I-10), climbing gently into the White Tank foothills. Coordinate is the OSM park centroid. The campsites are near the park entrance.
camps.priceTent: $20/night per campsite (7 sites, A to G). Each site has two 12x12 ft tent pads, a picnic table, a grill and a fire ring.
camps.reservations: Reservation required: request online or call Mon-Fri 9am-7pm. The city calls back within 72 hours to confirm and take payment, so same-day booking isn't realistic. Park hours are 5am-10pm.
camps.cyclistNotes: There's no drinking water anywhere in the park (the city says so explicitly), so carry it all in. Restrooms have sinks and toilets but no showers. It's only worth the 9-mile detour if you booked it a few days ahead.

camps.name: Leaf Verde Sun RV Community
camps.access: 1500 S Apache Rd, Buckeye, near I-10, about 4-5 miles north of the line on paved city streets.
camps.priceTent: No tent rate published. RV sites are $54-75/night on Hipcamp.
camps.reservations: Sun Communities park. Hipcamp is request-to-book. A 2024 review says the office is closed on weekends.
camps.cyclistNotes: Mostly long-term residents. Every current listing shows RV sites only, so call before detouring 4.5 miles. Old listings mentioned tents, but nothing confirms it now.

camps.name: 3Acre Desert RV Camp (Hipcamp)
camps.access: Private fenced 3-acre lot about 1 mile off the line, between Arlington and Wintersburg (address after booking). It borders a wash and State Trust land. Drive-in, 2WD access.
camps.priceTent: $25/night for an RV site (about $29.58 with Hipcamp fees). Tent use isn't listed, so ask the host.
camps.address: near Tonopah/Arlington, AZ (exact address after booking)
camps.reservations: Request-to-book, not instant. Message the host the day before. 1 booking so far, 100% recommend.
camps.cyclistNotes: Apart from Stage Stop, this is the only private option between Buckeye and Tonopah. The listing is RV-only, so get the host's OK to pitch a tent before counting on it. Potable water, fire pit and trash are listed.

camps.name: Buckeye Ranch RV Resort
camps.access: 105 N 339th Ave at I-10 exit 103, about 4-5 miles north of the Salome Hwy line on paved roads.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites. RV sites are $58+/night and cabins $102+/night on Hipcamp.
camps.reservations: Campspot/Hipcamp, request-to-book.
camps.cyclistNotes: New big-rig resort with full-hookup RV sites and cabins only, no tent sites. Listed here so you don't detour for it.

camps.name: Stage Stop RV Park / Wintersburg General Store
camps.access: 2614 S Wintersburg Rd, right at the line on Salome Hwy. The store is at the park entrance.
camps.priceTent: No tent rate. RV daily is $60 with utilities, plus a $300 refundable deposit on all lodging.
camps.reservations: Register at the Wintersburg General Store (open daily 5am-9pm; office Mon-Fri 6am-8pm, Sat-Sun 12-8pm). Rentals require a deposit and 2 IDs.
camps.cyclistNotes: Worker park for Palo Verde nuclear plant staff. Showers are for tenants. Tent policy is unknown, so ask at the store. The store itself is the key resupply on this stretch: groceries, fresh produce, fuel and an ATM, with Tin Top Bar & Grill on site.

camps.name: Saddle Mountain RV Park
camps.access: 40902 W Osborn Rd, half a mile south of I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave), on pavement.
camps.priceTent: Full-hookup sites are $50/night plus tax for 2 people. A Nov 2024 RoverPass listing showed tents at $30 (or $35 with power), but the 2026 operator site lists RV sites only.
camps.reservations: Call or email; $200 refundable deposit. Office is open Mon-Fri 9am-3pm (Sep-Apr). After hours, self check-in at the desk by the office door: pick a site from the board and pay by envelope.
camps.cyclistNotes: Reopened under new management after showing 'permanently closed' in 2023. Ask whether they'll put a tent on an RV site. Self check-in makes late arrival easy. Flies from nearby egg and chicken farms have been reported in the area.

camps.name: El Dorado Hot Spring
camps.access: 41225 W Indian School Rd, Tonopah, 0.3 mile on pavement from I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave).
camps.priceTent: About $50/night (Feb 2026 review; The Dyrt lists 'from $40'). Has primitive tent sites plus 30A electric sites.
camps.website: unknown (old eldoradohotspring.com no longer resolves; listings link to a Facebook page)
camps.address: 41225 W Indian School Rd, Tonopah, AZ 85354
camps.reservations: Call ahead. A March 2026 guest reported no check-in instructions and a double booking, so confirm by phone the same day.
camps.cyclistNotes: The one confirmed tent camp with showers at Tonopah. Outdoor showers and new restrooms were built in 2024. It's a clothing-optional hot spring with one 24/7 nude-only pool, and you can hear the interstate. Pilot, Chevron and Exxon are across exit 94.

camps.name: BLM land along Hovatter Rd (I-10 exit 53) - unverified fallback
camps.access: Take I-10 exit 53, then go south on Hovatter Rd. It's dirt and 'smooth but very sandy' at the start, so expect to push a loaded bike. The land is BLM Yuma Field Office until the Kofa NWR boundary about 20+ miles south. The coordinate is the road near the interchange, not a known campsite.
camps.priceTent: Free under the standard BLM rule (14 days in any 28) if the parcel is BLM.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the only spot right on the interstate between Tonopah and Quartzsite, about 41 miles from Tonopah. I found no camper reports. Check a land-status map (BLM vs State Trust) before pitching and stay well away from the freeway. Bouse Wash rest area (restrooms, water unreliable) is 1 mile west; the Pilot at exit 45 is 8 miles west.

camps.name: Gold Nugget Rd BLM dispersed (I-10 exit 26)
camps.access: I-10 exit 26 (Gold Nugget Rd), then south 1/4 mile. Loose small gravel and firm sand.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: The first free pitch right on the interstate after Tonopah, 7-8 miles before Quartzsite. Cactus debris means puncture risk (reviewers say it isn't dog-friendly), plus freeway hum and ATVs. BLM says short-term camping around Quartzsite is limited to five designated areas and this isn't one of them, so obey any 'no camping' signs (Scaddan Wash is 6 miles on). The newest review is Feb 2024.

camps.name: Scaddan Wash BLM 14-day camping area
camps.access: Leave I-10 at exit 19 (Riggles Ave) and ride about 1.5-2 miles east on Dome Rock Rd E (the south frontage road; rough, so reviewers use the shoulder) to the area. Inside it's dirt and sand with washes.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. A seasonal camp host registers campers.
camps.address: Dome Rock Rd E, Quartzsite, AZ 85346
camps.reservations: First-come; register with the host if present.
camps.cyclistNotes: The designated free area closest to town, within bike range of all Quartzsite services. Very loud near the freeway, so go well south. A Dec 2025 review reports dumped tires and a microwave.

camps.name: Plomosa Road BLM 14-day camping area
camps.access: About 5.5 miles north on US 95, then about 1-1.5 miles east on Plomosa Rd (busy by day). Graded gravel and small rock.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. A Feb 2026 review listed a $44 rate with no explanation; other reviews say free.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Quieter and less dusty than Hi Jolly or Dome Rock, but a 7-mile detour. Windy.

camps.name: Hi Jolly BLM 14-day camping area
camps.access: 3 miles north of Quartzsite on US 95 at milepost 112 (paved highway), gravel inside.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. Register with the camp host for a free 14-day pass when one is on duty.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Crowded with RVs in season, though clean. Camp toward the east side, away from US 95 noise. Water, dump and propane are in town, 3 miles away.

camps.name: Tumbleweed RV Park (Rose's RV Park)
camps.access: 600 Kuehn St, Quartzsite, next to I-10. City streets.
camps.priceTent: $8-40/night per The Dyrt, which lists 'Standard (tent/RV)' sites. Showers were coin-op ($5 in 2019) and free in 2023.
camps.reservations: Call; no online booking.
camps.cyclistNotes: The cheap end of its range may be a tent or dry spot. Constant I-10 noise. A 2019 reviewer rode a bike to town and the RV show from here.

camps.name: Quail Run RV Park
camps.access: 918 N Central Blvd, Quartzsite. City streets.
camps.priceTent: unknown
camps.cyclistNotes: RVezy lists tent sites, but AllStays lists it as 55+. Unverified; call or skip.

camps.name: 88 Shades RV Park - no tents
camps.access: 575 W Main St, Quartzsite.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites (RV $35/night).
camps.cyclistNotes: RV-only snowbird park. Earlier research and every current listing show RV sites only.

camps.name: Q View RV Park (formerly B-10 Campground)
camps.access: 615 W Main St in central Quartzsite, near I-10 exit 17/19. City streets.
camps.priceTent: $25/night 'Dry Camping', plus a $2.50 booking fee, a 3% card fee and tax ($125/week). Hookup sites are $35-50.
camps.phone: (928) 927-4393 (site says this line is temporarily down; temporary number 501-691-5757)
camps.reservations: Book online or call. Open 365 days.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the baseline 'B-10 Campground' under its new name. It offers dry camping 'for non-RV folks' (a guest review quoted on its site), private hot showers that aren't coin-op, Starlink Wi-Fi, laundry and fire pits. The old B-10 had numerous tent sites. Confirm the dry site takes a tent when you book. Walking distance to everything in town.

camps.name: La Posa LTVA (North/South/West/Tyson Wash)
camps.access: About 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US 95 (from I-10 exit 17), with four sub-areas. Permits are sold at the entrance host station. Dirt roads inside, reported rough after the 2026 flooding.
camps.priceTent: In season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days; there's no one-night rate. The long-term permit is $180. A 2024 BLM plan proposed $200/$600, but I found no sign it was adopted.
camps.reservations: First-come; buy the permit on site or at the Yuma Field Office.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only Quartzsite camp with public water taps (8, though a reviewer calls the water salty, so carry drinking water), 10 vault toilets, dump and trash. Poor value for one night next to the free 14-day areas.

camps.name: Desert Gardens RV Park (Sky Resorts)
camps.access: 1240 Acacia Rd, south-west Quartzsite. City streets.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. RV sites start at $36/night (Good Sam).
camps.reservations: Book online or call. Open year-round.
camps.cyclistNotes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator site advertises full-hookup RV sites only and AllStays calls it 55+. Call first.

camps.name: Road Runner BLM 14-day camping area
camps.access: About 6 miles south of I-10 on US 95 to milepost 99, then just west via N 53rd St / La Paz Valley Rd. Hard-packed gravel, with a steep drop-off at the road edge.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. A host issues free permits in season.
camps.address: La Paz Valley Rd, Quartzsite, AZ 85346
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Huge and nearly empty in late Oct 2025. Go west, away from US 95 traffic. Note it's a 12-mile round trip off the westbound route.

camps.name: Dome Rock Mountain BLM 14-day camping area
camps.access: On the westbound route: Dome Rock Rd W (south frontage road), 3-5 miles west of town. Rocky but passable dirt. The camp host is near the entrance. Coordinates vary by source (Campendium 33.6494,-114.2715; The Dyrt 33.6409,-114.3151); the area is large.
camps.priceTent: Free. Get the free 14-day permit from the seasonal camp host.
camps.reservations: First-come; register with the host.
camps.cyclistNotes: Up to about 400 sites on hard, flat desert. Load all water in Quartzsite. Stay out of the marked gas-pipeline corridor. It's just past the segment end (mile ~176-178) and already on the road to Blythe, so it's the natural first night west of town.

camps.name: Saddle Mountain BLM dispersed camping
camps.access: The Salome variant runs right past it on W Courthouse Rd, paved from the east. Many entrances; a popular one is near Courthouse Rd mile marker 13. Sites sit on rocky, rutted dirt spurs (coordinate is approximate). From the main I-10 line it's about 8-10 riding miles SW of exit 94 via Indian School Rd, Saddle Vista Rd, Salome Hwy and Courthouse Rd. Don't follow GPS onto Salome Hwy from I-10 exit 81: it's dirt until Courthouse Rd.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14 days in any 28.
camps.reservations: First-come, no permit or host.
camps.cyclistNotes: Fill water at Tonopah (exit 94) or the Saddle Vista Ranch RV fill (about 10c/gal per a 2024 review). Reviews from Oct 26-27, 2026 call the fly swarms 'unbearable' (nearby egg/chicken farms), so expect them in early November. Also: weekend target shooting, rocky ground (bring stakes that hold in gravel), and a power-plant smell on some winds.

camps.name: Indian Hills RV Resort
camps.access: 67668 Salome Rd, on paved Salome Rd at the SE edge of Salome. The variant passes the gate.
camps.priceTent: $39.20/night on Hipcamp for a 50x55 ft back-in 'RV/tent' site with full hookups and 30/50A (about $48.78 with fees). A furnished teepee is $85, casitas $125+.
camps.reservations: Hipcamp instant book (same-day OK, 1-night minimum) or call. Office hours aren't published.
camps.cyclistNotes: The best-equipped tent stop on the variant: hot showers, laundry, free Wi-Fi, a store and fitness room, all ages. It's the first camp after the 41-mile empty Harquahala Valley stretch. 13 Hipcamp bookings, 100% recommend.

camps.name: Centennial Park (La Paz County)
camps.access: 69725 Centennial Park Rd, about 3 miles east of Salome off US 60 (toward Wenden). Gravel park roads.
camps.priceTent: $10/night dry camping, or $20 with water and electric (May 2025 review). Dump is $10.
camps.reservations: First-come with an on-site host (2022). Late-arrival rules unknown.
camps.cyclistNotes: The cheapest legal pitch around Salome, plus a desert golf course. Facilities have been unreliable: 2018 and 2021 reviews mention showers, but in 2022 the restrooms were locked (porta-potties) and the well water was not drinkable. Call before relying on its water or showers.

camps.name: Salome KOA Journey
camps.access: 64812 Harcuvar Dr, just off US 60 about 2.5 miles west of Salome (near milepost 54). The variant line passes the entrance. KOA's own directions say 'US 60 to MP 54, then 2 mi S on Harcuvar Dr', but mapped coordinates put the park about 0.2 mile from US 60.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. KOA lists Deluxe and Premium tent sites; Good Sam mentions a gravel overflow tent area. RV sites start around $51/night (Good Sam).
camps.reservations: Online, KOA app or phone. Office is roughly 8am-4pm daily, with lit after-hours check-in. Open all year.
camps.cyclistNotes: Pool, hot tub, laundry and a camp store. Salome Restaurant is about 0.2 mile away on US 60. New owners (the Johnston family, Dec 2025) are restoring a breakfast kitchen.

camps.name: Ramblin' Roads RV Resort (Hope)
camps.access: 60655 US 60 at Hope. The variant goes by the door.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. The Dyrt lists sites 'from free to $35/night'.
camps.reservations: Call or email. Arriving late: fill out an envelope at the after-hours registration on the front of the building (lobby open until 9pm). After 9pm, take any open site and pay when the lobby opens at 9am. Office Mon-Sat 9am-2pm, Oct 1 to Apr 1.
camps.cyclistNotes: The operator's amenity list explicitly includes TENT CAMPING (plus good well water and free Wi-Fi), but it's a 55+ park. Confirm they'll take your party before relying on it.

camps.name: Vicksburg Pit Rd BLM dispersed
camps.access: From Vicksburg Junction (US 60, variant mile about 66.5), about 2-3 miles north toward SR 72 and Vicksburg to Vicksburg Pit Rd. The access is wide, well-graded gravel; cross the railroad tracks slowly. From the main I-10 line: exit 45 (mile about 145), then about 8 miles north on Vicksburg Rd.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Quiet, few campers and dark skies (Feb 2026 reviews). Flies even in December. The BLM land borders private parcels, so stay on BLM. No services: get water at the Pilot at I-10 exit 45 or in Salome.

camps.name: Steve and Dawn Desert Getaway
camps.access: 10 fenced acres north of US 60 near Vicksburg; GPS may show Salome. About 5.6 miles in a straight line north of the variant, probably on dirt roads. Address comes with the booking.
camps.priceTent: $15-30/night. There are 3 dry sites for tent or RV (no water or power at the site) and 2 full-hookup RV sites.
camps.reservations: Request to Book through The Dyrt.
camps.cyclistNotes: The listing says there is 'as yet no bathroom on-site'. It's far off the line, so only worth it if everything closer is full.

camps.name: 3 Dreamers RV Park
camps.access: 54000 US 60, about 3 miles west of Vicksburg Junction, right on the variant.
camps.priceTent: $32/night per The Dyrt (probably the RV rate). No tent rate on the operator site.
camps.reservations: Call. Office and campstore are open Mon-Sat 11am-5pm (Oct-Mar), closed Sunday. A Dec 2025 review says the owners helped with a late-night arrival.
camps.cyclistNotes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator's site mentions only full-hookup RV sites. Call first. New owners in 2025; clean hot showers, laundry, campstore and propane.

camps.name: The Collier 15 (Hipcamp)
camps.access: Fenced 55-acre property just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda (address after booking). Short dirt driveway.
camps.priceTent: $22.75/night (about $26.79 with Hipcamp fees) for an RV/tent site with full hookups and a 30A outlet. Two sites: 'The 2 mesquites' (concrete pad, fire pit) and 'The Willow'.
camps.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice. 17 bookings, 86% recommend.
camps.cyclistNotes: The host calls it 'perfect for tent camping', and you get an outlet to charge. A toilet is listed but no shower. Buckaroos store in Brenda is about 5 miles west. Same host as The Dusty 40 next door.

camps.name: The Dusty 40 (Hipcamp)
camps.access: 40-acre desert parcel next to The Collier 15, just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda. Dirt access.
camps.priceTent: $8/night (about $11 with fees). Pitch anywhere on the property.
camps.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum. 5 bookings, 100% recommend.
camps.cyclistNotes: Bare land the host is still cleaning up, with broken glass in spots, so watch your tires and tent floor. Bring all water.

camps.name: Black Rock RV Village (Brenda)
camps.access: 46751 E US 60 in Brenda, on the variant, 3.7 miles before it rejoins I-10 at exit 31.
camps.priceTent: No tent rate. RV sites are $40-45/night.
camps.reservations: Office closes at 3pm and is closed Sundays.
camps.cyclistNotes: Lists RV sites only, so ask about a tent before counting on it. Black Rock Cafe on site (limited hours) and Buckaroos Country Store nearby make Brenda a food stop either way. Wi-Fi only works at the diner and pavilion.

camps.name: Desert Gold RV Resort (Brenda) - no tents
camps.access: 46628 US 60, Brenda.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites.
camps.cyclistNotes: Reviewers on The Dyrt report the rule 'No tents or backpacking.' Listed so you skip it. Buckaroos Country Store and Black Rock Cafe are next door in Brenda.

camps.name: Ramsey Mine Rd BLM dispersed
camps.access: Ramsey Mine Rd runs south from US 60 about 1 mile west of Brenda and crosses over I-10 on a bridge (no interchange). Camp along the smaller parallel gravel road on flat, hard ground. From the main I-10 line: exit 31 (mile about 159.5), then about 3.5 miles east on US 60 and south.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
camps.reservations: First-come.
camps.cyclistNotes: Room for 40-50 rigs, rarely more than 15 (Jan 2026). About 1 mile from Buckaroos Country Store (groceries, sandwiches) and Black Rock Cafe in Brenda. OHVs raise dust on Ramsey Mine Rd itself, and I-10 hum starts around 6am. Fires only Oct-Mar; no wood gathering.

research.waterAndFood:
MAIN I-10 LINE (corridor miles from Casa Grande, measured on the app's line):
- Buckeye (~70.6): full services.
- Wintersburg General Store at Stage Stop RV Park, mile ~88.5, on the line: open daily 5am-9pm, with groceries, fresh produce, fuel and an ATM. Tin Top Bar & Grill is next door.
- Tonopah, I-10 exit 94 (~95.9): Pilot, Chevron and Exxon, plus a Dollar General and mini mart in town.
- Burnt Well rest area, MP 86 (~103.7): restrooms and a water spigot (reported 2024), recently renovated.
- Bouse Wash rest area, MP ~52 (~137.8): restrooms, but water 'may not always be available' and there was none in Jan 2025.
- I-10 exit 45, Vicksburg Rd (~145.0): Pilot open 24 hours with food, restrooms and showers (928-859-3165), plus a Pacific Pride fuel stop.
- Exit 31 / US 60 (~159.5): Brenda is 3.7 mi off, with Buckaroos Country Store (groceries, sandwich shop) and Black Rock Cafe (limited hours).
- Quartzsite (~171-174): everything.
Longest main-line stretch without guaranteed water is Burnt Well rest area to exit 45, about 41 mi, because Bouse Wash's tap is unreliable. If Burnt Well is dry too, it's Tonopah to exit 45, about 49 mi.

SALOME VARIANT (its own miles from Tonopah = 0):
- Tonopah: stores at exit 94. Saddle Vista Ranch near the start sells RV water at about 10c/gal (2024 review).
- Harquahala Valley: nothing.
- Salome (~52.9-54): Indian Hills RV Resort store, RZ Mini Mart/VP Racing and a Mobil on US 60. Salome Restaurant is at ~58.4 next to the KOA, which also has a camp store.
- Hope (~62.7) and Vicksburg Junction (~66.5): no store confirmed. The Pilot at I-10 exit 45 is about 6 mi south of Vicksburg Junction.
- Brenda (~77): Buckaroos Country Store and Black Rock Cafe.
- Then I-10 into Quartzsite (~93-95).
Longest variant stretch with no confirmed water or food is Tonopah to Salome, about 53 mi, so carry 6+ liters. A tip (distances not verified on the ground): riding I-10 from exit 94 to exit 81 (13 mi) passes the Burnt Well rest area tap and rejoins the variant at the Salome Rd/Harquahala Valley Rd crossing at variant mile ~21. That saves about 8 mi but skips Saddle Mountain BLM.
research.legality:
BIKES ON I-10: ADOT's Traffic Engineering Guideline 1030 (the Jan 2018 table the workflow downloaded) bans bicycles on I-10 only from MP 114.86 (Miller Rd, Buckeye) to MP 270.59 (Kolb Rd, Tucson). The route's I-10 use from Tonopah (exit 94) west through Quartzsite and on to California is legal; the line avoids the banned Phoenix stretch by using Baseline Rd and Salome Hwy. I did not verify shoulder widths.

ROADWORK AND DAMAGE:
- ADOT guardrail repair on eastbound I-10 at MP 89-90 ran Oct 14-15, 2026 and is done.
- A Burnt Well rest area truck-parking expansion starts in December 2026; ADOT says the rest area stays open.
- Earlier ADOT paving projects (Salome Rd to Tonopah, roughly MP 80-90; Dome Rock Rd to Scaddan Wash, MP 11-24) brought night lane closures. Check az511.gov for active closures that take the shoulder.
- On Aug 12, 2026 a 2-4 inch flash flood closed I-10 at Quartzsite for hours and ran through RV parks on the east side of town. A reviewer reports La Posa North LTVA roads rough after the 2026 flooding.

VARIANT ROADS: Indian School Rd, Saddle Vista Rd, W Courthouse Rd (reported paved from the east), Harquahala Valley Rd, Salome Rd and US 60 are two-lane rural roads. I didn't confirm that Salome Rd is paved end to end. Don't follow GPS onto W Salome Hwy from I-10 exit 81: it's dirt until Courthouse Rd.

CAMPING LAW:
- Wildlife areas: Arizona Game & Fish rule A.A.C. R12-4-802 (current Supp. 26-2, June 30, 2026) says 'No overnight public camping' on the Arlington, Powers Butte (Mumme Farm), Robbins Butte and Base & Meridian wildlife areas. Those are the Gila River lands along the Buckeye-Arlington stretch of the main line, so don't stealth-camp there.
- ADOT rest areas (Burnt Well MP 86, Bouse Wash MP ~52) allow parking and sleeping in a vehicle, reportedly one night only, not tents.
- Truck stops are not tent-legal.
- BLM: free dispersed camping is allowed for 14 days in any 28 unless posted; after that you must move more than 25 mi.
- Quartzsite: BLM Yuma Field Office says short-term camping around Quartzsite is limited to five designated free 14-day areas (Hi Jolly, Plomosa Rd, Scaddan Wash, Road Runner, Dome Rock), plus the fee La Posa LTVA. Seasonal camp hosts register campers for free. Gold Nugget Rd (exit 26) is outside that list, so obey any signs.
- La Posa LTVA in season (Sept 15-Apr 15) needs the $40 14-day short-visit permit; there's no nightly fee. BLM's 2024 proposal to raise LTVA fees hasn't been confirmed as adopted.
- Arizona State Trust land needs a recreation permit ($15/yr individual, land.az.gov) and allows 14 camping nights per calendar year.

NOT FOUND: no casino, church or community site on this segment documents tent camping or cyclist hosting.
research.gapWarnings:
MAIN I-10 LINE, TONOPAH TO QUARTZSITE (the critical gap): from El Dorado Hot Spring / Tonopah (mile ~95.6) to the Gold Nugget Rd BLM pull-off at exit 26 (mile ~163.5) is about 68 mi with no confirmed tent-legal camp within 10 mi of the interstate. The rest areas (Burnt Well MP 86, Bouse Wash MP ~52) and the exit-45 truck stops are NOT tent-legal. On a 50-mile wind day out of Tonopah you'd be near exit 45 (mile ~145, 49 mi). Fallbacks within 20 mi:
- Exit 45, then 8-11 mi north on Vicksburg Rd / US 60 to: Vicksburg Pit Rd BLM (free, ~8 mi), 3 Dreamers RV (Dyrt lists tent sites, ~9 mi), The Collier 15 ($27 Hipcamp, outlet, ~11 mi), The Dusty 40 ($11, ~11 mi), or Ramblin' Roads in Hope (55+, tents, ~10 mi).
- Exit 31 (mile ~159.5), then about 3.5-4 mi to Ramsey Mine Rd BLM.
- Unverified, sandy BLM land along Hovatter Rd at exit 53 (mile ~136.5).
- Saddle Mountain BLM, 8-10 mi SW of exit 94, but only at the Tonopah end.

THE SALOME VARIANT FIXES THIS: it is about 18 mi longer (81.4 mi from Tonopah to its I-10 rejoin at exit 31, vs 63.6 mi on I-10). After Salome it has a tent-legal camp every 6 mi or less. Its own gap is Saddle Mountain BLM (variant mile ~9-12) to Indian Hills RV Resort (mile 52.9), about 41 mi. That's Harquahala Valley farmland and State Trust land with no camp and no water; the only legal fallback is an Arizona State Trust recreation permit on an unposted trust parcel.

BUCKEYE TO TONOPAH (main line): about 26 mi between the Sunset Nooks (mile 69.7) and El Dorado Hot Spring (mile 95.6). Fine, but the in-between options are unconfirmed for tents: 3Acre Desert RV Camp (Hipcamp, RV-only listing) and Stage Stop RV Park (tent policy unknown).

QUARTZSITE: free tent-legal options are Scaddan Wash, Hi Jolly, Plomosa Rd, Road Runner and Dome Rock. Most of the roughly 40 private RV parks are RV-only and/or 55+. Confirmed or likely tent-friendly: Q View RV Park (the old B-10) at $25 dry camping with showers. Unverified: Tumbleweed/Rose's, Desert Gardens, Quail Run. No tents: 88 Shades.

CONFIRMED NO-TENT OR RV-ONLY, so don't detour: Desert Gold RV Resort (Brenda), Buckeye Ranch RV Resort, 88 Shades. Also RV-only: Desert Oasis RV Parking (Salome) and Boots' Corral (Hipcamp hookup only). Not checked for tents (search budget ran out), and mostly listed as 55+: Wagon West, Gateway Ranch, Brenda RV Park, Gold Fever Adventures, Desert Gem, Sunset RV Park, Desert Palms, and Park Place RV Park in Quartzsite.

RESEARCH NOTE: the shared web-search budget ran out partway through. Coverage after that point came from direct fetches of operator, BLM, Hipcamp, Campendium and Dyrt pages plus OSM/Nominatim, so a few small private parks above stay unverified.

camps.name: Scaddan Wash BLM 14-Day Camping Area
camps.address: Dome Rock Rd E (south frontage), east of I-10 exit 19, Quartzsite, AZ 85346
camps.access: Leave I-10 at exit 19 (Riggles Ave), then take the south-side frontage road (Dome Rock Rd E) east about 1.5 mi to the BLM sign. Inside are gravel and dirt tracks off Mitchell Mine Rd. Ordinary vehicles get in fine.
camps.priceTent: Free, 14 days in any 28
camps.reservations: First come, first served, at any hour. Check in with the camp host if one is posted.
camps.cyclistNotes: This is the closest free BLM area to town (about 10 minutes' drive) and the first one a westbound rider reaches, just before Quartzsite. You can hear I-10 near the entrance, so ride further south for quiet. Reviews from Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 confirm it is still free and in use. There is no water: fill up at the exit-19 Chevron/ARCO, where OSM maps a public tap.

camps.name: Park Place RV Park
camps.access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then 0.4 mi north on Riggles Ave.
camps.priceTent: No tents. RV night is $45 + tax.
camps.reservations: Book by phone. Register and prepay on arrival.
camps.cyclistNotes: The posted park rules say 'No tents' and full-hookup RVs only, with a 10-year age limit on rigs. Don't plan on it.

camps.name: Quartzsite RV Resort
camps.access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then north on Riggles Ave.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. A full-hookup RV night is $55 in November 2026.
camps.reservations: OSM gives reception hours of 8am to 7pm. Call ahead.
camps.cyclistNotes: A small park with 27 full-hookup RV sites. The website mentions only RV sites, so ask before counting on a tent.

camps.name: Arizona Sun RV Park
camps.access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then 1/2 mi north on Plymouth Ave and 1/4 mi on Quail Trail.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. A daily RV site is $47 + $6.20 tax.
camps.reservations: Call for reservations. Check-in is at 1 PM.
camps.cyclistNotes: 126 full-hookup sites with shower houses and laundry. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but the operator only lists RV rates, so call. The park is across the street from BLM desert.

camps.name: Desert Edge RV Park
camps.access: Paved, near I-10 exit 19.
camps.priceTent: unknown
camps.reservations: OSM says reservations are recommended. Call.
camps.cyclistNotes: The park's domain (desertedgervpark.com) now redirects to a parking page, so it may have changed hands. Its status is unverified.

camps.name: Pattie's RV Park & Propane
camps.access: On paved E Main St (Business 10), between exits 19 and 17.
camps.priceTent: unknown
camps.reservations: Small park, call ahead.
camps.cyclistNotes: A small park with back-in full-hookup sites, a smoothie and coffee bar, and laundry (2021 review). It also rents trailers. No tent information.

camps.name: Rice Ranch North
camps.access: Paved streets in town, a block south of Main St.

camps.name: Tumbleweed RV Park
camps.access: Paved streets in town, south of Main St near I-10.
camps.priceTent: The Dyrt lists $8–$40. Tent rate unknown.
camps.reservations: Call.
camps.cyclistNotes: Has both dry-camping and full-hookup sites, flush toilets and showers. Showers were $5 for anyone in 2019 and free for guests in 2023. Worth a call for a cheap tent spot. The Dyrt record says no tents, but that may just be missing data.

camps.name: Crawford's RV Park
camps.access: On paved E Main St (Business 10).
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. Off-season daily RV site is $45 + tax (2026–27 rates).
camps.reservations: Reservations by phone. The park says overnighters are welcome.
camps.cyclistNotes: 67 full-hookup sites, laundry and a rental cabin. The site never mentions tents, so call.

camps.name: Rice Ranch RV Park
camps.access: Paved streets in town.
camps.priceTent: No tents. RV sites run $42–79.
camps.reservations: Online or by phone.
camps.cyclistNotes: The operator's FAQ says it 'does not offer dry camping or tent sites'. Every stay must be on a full-hookup RV site.

camps.name: Texas BBQ RV Park
camps.address: Quartzsite, AZ (on Main St near I-10)
camps.access: Paved, in town.
camps.priceTent: unknown
