research.waterAndFood:
Mileages use the task's anchors (Quartzsite 173.6, Blythe 197.4). Quartzsite (mi ~170–174.5) has full services. The exit-19 Chevron is open 24/7 and OSM maps a public water tap at the ARCO there. Main St has Roadrunner Market, Coyote Fresh Foods, Dollar General Market, Big Market, Silly Al's Pizza, McDonald's and Carl's Jr., and Pilot and Terrible's are open 24/7. Love's at exit 17 (mi ~174.4) is the last stop westbound. RV parks and the La Posa South and Tyson Wash LTVA stations also have water.

West of town, the I-10 shoulder has nothing until the Ehrenberg rest area (I-10 milepost 4, mi ~187.9), which has water and restrooms and is open 24 hours. The regenerated line stays on I-10, so the rest area is now directly on route. Next is the Flying J travel center with a Wendy's at Ehrenberg exit 1 (mi ~193.1). It is open 24/7, and BLM says it gives free potable water. A 76 station with a Fatburger and a Family Dollar sit next door.

Blythe (mi ~194–200) has full services along Hobsonway: Shell and Mobil at the east end (~195.8), Dollar General, Smart & Final, Albertsons (6am–11pm, ~198) and the Lovekin Blvd cluster (~199), which includes 24 Market (5am–11:30pm).

Longest stretches inside this segment: about 13.5 mi without water (Love's to the rest area) and about 18.7 mi without food (Love's to the Flying J). Every BLM camp here is dry. Carry 4–6 L from Quartzsite for Scaddan Wash, Hi Jolly, Dome Rock, Road Runner or Plomosa, and from the Flying J for the Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, Sandbowl or Levee Rd sites.

The critical one comes just past this segment: Blythe is the last real resupply before a 49–59 mi stretch with no food westbound. The last store is BB Travel Center/Chevron at exit 232, and Wiley's Well rest area (exit 222) is the last water before Chiriaco Summit. Leave Blythe with 5 L or more.
research.legality:
The app's line changed while I was researching. data/corridors/lines.json was regenerated around 22:33 on Nov 1. The new line rides I-10 for the whole 16.5 mi from Quartzsite to Ehrenberg exit 1, instead of Dome Rock Rd W plus Tom Wells Rd, and the anchors moved: Quartzsite is now mi 185.6, Ehrenberg exit 1 mi 203.6 and Blythe mi 207.8. My corridor miles use the task's anchors (Quartzsite 173.6, Blythe 197.4). To convert to the new line, add about 12.0 near Quartzsite and about 10.4–10.5 at Ehrenberg and Blythe, or re-project from lat/lng.

Arizona: bikes are legal on all of I-10 west of Miller Rd under ADOT policy TGP 1030. That covers Quartzsite, the Dome Rock pass and Ehrenberg exit 1, which is signed US Bicycle Route 90. Dome Rock Rd W is paved with no shoulder and is the access road for the Dome Rock BLM camp (exit 17 to exit 11). Tom Wells Rd is about 4 mi of compacted dirt (OSM).

The I-10 shoulder from Dome Rock to Ehrenberg is fairly wide but strewn with shredded-tire steel wire, screws and bungee cords (an eastbound 2025 rider), so run sealant and carry spare tubes. Westbound it's about 11 mi of mostly gentle descent from roughly 1,200 ft to the river at about 300 ft. ADOT has a Dome Rock Rd–Scaddan Wash paving project with night lane closures; I couldn't confirm its dates.

Crossing the Colorado River: a separate bike and foot bridge beside I-10 (OSM cycleway 314745291, part of US Bicycle Route 90) lands on E Hobsonway. Riders have also used the I-10 bridge, and a 2025 group reported a bike lane on it. Caltrans District 8 data lists I-10 as closed to bikes from Mesa Dr (exit 232) to the Arizona line, so ride Hobsonway / Hobson Way through Blythe to the Mesa Dr on-ramp. Westbound I-10 has the California agricultural inspection station at Riviera Dr (exit 243), so don't carry fresh produce. Caltrans's I-10 Blythe repaving (Wiley's Well to the state line, due to finish winter 2026) means lane shifts near the bridge. Clocks go back an hour entering California.

Camp access roads:
- US 95 north and south of Quartzsite, and asphalt Plomosa Rd: paved.
- Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd: compacted gravel (OSM grade 2), washboarded for about 2 mi.
- The Sandbowl: very soft sand.
- Levee Rd: 8–12 mi of rough washboard dirt.
- Intake Blvd, 6th Ave and Colorado River Rd to Mayflower; S Intake Blvd and Peter D McIntyre Ave to McIntyre: paved.

Near Quartzsite, camp only inside the BLM's signed 14-day areas or the LTVAs (BLM designates these locations). Respect the posted Day Use Only zones and the pipeline strip at Dome Rock. California does not allow city-park camping, and Blythe has no free legal camping inside town.
research.gapWarnings:
No stretch in mi 172–200 goes more than 30 mi without a tent-legal camp. On-line spacing, using the task's anchors:
- Scaddan Wash BLM (free), at mi ~170.2.
- Quartzsite town, mi ~171–174: Q View dry camping at $25 (the former B-10, tents probable), Tyson Wells at $25 (tents probable), the La Posa LTVA ($40 permit), and free BLM at Hi Jolly, Road Runner and Plomosa, 3.8–6.5 mi off.
- Dome Rock BLM (free), mi ~176.4–178.5.
- Then 14.5 mi on I-10 over the Dome Rock pass with nothing tent-legal I could verify near exits 11 or 5.
- Ehrenberg exit 1, mi ~193.0: Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd BLM (free, 3.5 mi off) and the Sandbowl (soft sand). The Cove RV Resort is just across the river at mi ~193.6, with tents probable.
- Blythe at Intake Blvd, mi ~195.8: Mayflower County Park and McIntyre RV Resort, each about 6.7 mi off, both confirmed tent sites with showers.

The longest gap is Dome Rock to Ehrenberg, about 14.5 mi.

Fallbacks if the paid parks are full or the offices are closed (Q View 9–4 Arizona time; the Cove 8–5 and McIntyre 7–4 California time): Dome Rock or Scaddan Wash on the Quartzsite side, and Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd on the Arizona riverbank. All are free and open at any hour.

Things that won't work:
- Midland LTVA and Hidden Beaches ban tents.
- Most Quartzsite RV parks are RV-only. Quail Run, Rice Ranch, Scenic Road and Park Place explicitly ban tents, and Burrwood, JR's and Kofa Mountain are age-55-plus parks.
- The B-10 Campground entry in the app is stale. It is now Q View RV Park at the same address and phone.
- I found no Hipcamp listings in Quartzsite, Ehrenberg or Blythe (Hipcamp has no town pages there), and no church, casino or community site that documents hosting cyclists.

Watch the next segment, I10-D. West of Blythe, the next tent option appears to be Wiley's Well / Coon Hollow (Mule Mountain LTVA), about 9 mi south of I-10 exit 222. A $40 La Posa permit covers every LTVA in Arizona and California for 14 days. Nothing else on Blythe → Desert Center was checked here.

Method note: the shared web-search budget was already used up when this task started. This research used direct fetches of operator sites, BLM pages, Campendium, The Dyrt, Campspot, OpenStreetMap (Overpass and Nominatim), OSRM routing, and the app's own corridor files. Treat the 'unknown' tent policies at in-town Quartzsite RV parks as call-first.

camps.name: Mayflower Regional Park (Riverside County Parks)
camps.access: Paved and flat; reviewers say there is pavement all the way. Leave Hobsonway in Blythe at Intake Blvd/US 95 and ride north-east to the river at the end of 6th Ave/Colorado River Rd, about 7.8 mi each way by the bike router. Groceries in Blythe on the way.
camps.priceTent: Not readable: the county site blocks bots. A water/electric RV site averaged $49/night in Sept 2026 (Campendium review). The 27 dry/tent sites are the cheaper tier; hot showers are free.
camps.reservations: Riverside County Parks reservation site (reserve.rivcoparks.org) or call the park. A staffed gate/office checks campers in, and the stay limit is 14 nights. Late-arrival rules unknown, so call ahead if you will arrive after dark.
camps.cyclistNotes: The best full-service tent option at the Blythe end. Besides the hookup side it has a separate 'tent area'/dry-camp side, which a 2023 review found practically empty: grass under trees, with riverfront picnic tables. Hot showers are free. There is only one restroom building and it is far from some sites (one reviewer biked to it). Spigots are frequent but the water tastes mineral. Snowbird long-termers fill the hookup side in winter. A review dated Oct 18, 2026 found it open, clean and quiet. The cost is a ~15-mi round-trip detour off the line.

camps.name: McIntyre RV Resort (formerly Destiny McIntyre, Peter McIntyre County Park)
camps.address: 8750 E Peter D McIntyre Ave, Blythe, CA 92225
camps.access: Paved and flat. From Hobsonway in Blythe, head south on Intake Blvd through farmland to the river at Peter McIntyre Ave, about 7.4-7.8 mi each way.
camps.priceTent: $38/night 'Preferred Tent Camping' or $43 'Beach Front Tent Camping' (Campspot listing, Nov 2026), plus tax/fees. Restrooms and hot showers are included. Tent sites have no power; 30-amp riverfront RV sites are $50.
camps.reservations: Book on Campspot (campspot.com/park/mcintyre-rv-resort-blythe-ca, which shows live availability; 28 tent sites) or call. There is a camp store on site. Check-in hours not published.
camps.cyclistNotes: Confirmed tent sites on grass by the water. Showers and bathrooms are newly renovated; there is a store (ice, snacks), marine gas/propane and free Wi-Fi. New owners took over June 1, 2025. Campspot reviews from Aug 2026 ('Nice tent camping by the water') and Oct 2026 ('quiet, clean') confirm it is operating. Expect river partiers on weekends. It is a ~15-mi round trip off the line, like Mayflower.

camps.name: The Cove RV Resort (formerly Riviera RV Resort)
camps.access: Paved, 0.5 mi. It sits on the river just north of the first Blythe exit (Riviera Dr) after the Colorado River bridge.
camps.priceTent: Unknown. The 2026 website lists only RV sites at $60/night plus Blythe's 10% occupancy tax. Campendium's old 'tent camping: yes' tag is unconfirmed.
camps.reservations: Call to book. The office is open 8am-5pm daily; the general store 8-5 Sun-Thu and 8-6 Fri-Sat. A 2020 reviewer was given a site at 9:30 pm.
camps.cyclistNotes: The closest RV park to the line at Blythe; ask whether a tent can use an RV site. It has a pool and spa, renovated showers, coin laundry, and new Wi-Fi in 2026. It is 2.5 mi before this segment's start (mi 196), so it may duplicate the Quartzsite-Blythe segment.

camps.name: Hidden Beaches Resort (no tents)
camps.access: Paved, about 7.3 mi north-east of central Blythe on the river.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites: the website says 'All camping units must be self contained'. RV sites are about $51/night (Feb 2026).
camps.reservations: Call or email; the office opens at 8 am.
camps.cyclistNotes: Not a tent option. It is mostly a long-term/full-time park, and a Feb 2026 review complained about upkeep and showers.

camps.name: Burton's Mobile Home & R.V. Park (no tents)
camps.access: On Hobsonway, right on the line.
camps.priceTent: No tents: OpenStreetMap tags it tents=no. RV rates unknown.
camps.reservations: unknown
camps.cyclistNotes: A mobile-home park with some RV spaces and no tent sites listed. Treat it as unavailable for a tent.

camps.name: Midland LTVA (BLM) - no tents
camps.address: Midland Rd, 8 mi north of Blythe, CA 92225
camps.access: Paved: north from Blythe on Lovekin Blvd, then Midland Rd, about 8.5 mi each way.
camps.priceTent: Tents not allowed. Season permits (Sept 15-Apr 15) cost $40 per 14 days or $180, and here they are valid only for self-contained units.
camps.reservations: Permit from the on-site host or a BLM office.
camps.cyclistNotes: BLM rule: 'Short-term camping without self-containment is not allowed within the Midland LTVA camp sites.' It has no toilets and no water, only a dump station and trash. Not usable by a tent camper.

camps.name: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area)
camps.address: Wiley's Well Rd at I-10 exit 222 (north side), 15 mi west of Blythe
camps.access: Leave I-10 at exit 222. The Wiley's Well Rest Area sits on Wiley's Well Rd just north of the freeway. Ride a few hundred yards north on paved Wiley's Well Rd, or along the dirt powerline track parallel to I-10, and camp on open BLM desert out of sight of the road. Flat, firm ground.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit. No LTVA permit is needed because this is outside the Mule Mountain LTVA. Water and flush toilets are at the rest area 0.3 mi away, 24 h.
camps.reservations: None. You may NOT sleep inside the rest area itself: Caltrans has an 8-hour limit and no tents.
camps.cyclistNotes: Not a documented campsite; legal by land status. The BLM surface-management map shows BLM on every side of the interchange, inside Chuckwalla National Monument, and OSM shows no solar fencing here. It is the only spot between Blythe and Chiriaco where a dry camp sits beside water and toilets. It is 10 mi past the last store (BB Travel Center, exit 232) and 50 mi before Chiriaco. Two state prisons are 3 mi south, so stay north of I-10. Check for 'closed to camping' signs. Caltrans plans a rest-area water rebuild with no dates announced.

camps.name: Wiley's Well Campground (Mule Mountain LTVA, BLM)
camps.address: Wiley's Well Rd, 9 mi south of I-10 exit 222
camps.access: Exit 222, then south on Wiley's Well Rd: 3 mi paved past the Chuckwalla Valley and Ironwood state prisons, then 6 mi of graded dirt that is normally washboarded. BLM notice dated Oct 15, 2026: the road was damaged by Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, is 'impassable for RVs and trailers', and is 4x4 only. A loaded bike will be slow, with possible walking. 18 mi round trip.
camps.priceTent: $40 LTVA short-visit permit, required Sept 15-Apr 15. It covers 14 consecutive days at any CA/AZ LTVA; there is no nightly rate.
camps.reservations: No reservations. Buy the permit from the camp host (not always present) or a BLM office. Tents are allowed only at designated sites within 500 ft of the vault toilet.
camps.cyclistNotes: A real campground with tables, fire rings, a very clean vault toilet, trash and a dump station, but NO water; bring it from the rest area 9 mi back. Coon Hollow, 3 mi further south on the same damaged road, takes the same permit. Probably not worth the detour this week.

camps.name: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange)
camps.address: Corn Springs Rd / Chuckwalla Valley Rd at I-10 exit 201, 9 mi east of Desert Center
camps.access: Exit 201, south side. Paved Chuckwalla Valley Rd meets Corn Springs Rd at the ramps; go a few hundred yards west of Corn Springs Rd onto BLM desert. Keep clear of the fenced Maverick Solar project north and east of the exit.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map, inside Chuckwalla National Monument). It saves the sandy 7.8-mi ride to Corn Springs campground. A dry camp: the nearest water is Wiley's Well RA, 21 mi back, or Chiriaco, 29 mi ahead. Small dirt service roads (pipeline/utility) criss-cross the area.

camps.name: Corn Springs Campground (BLM)
camps.address: Corn Springs Rd, Chuckwalla Mountains, Desert Center, CA 92239
camps.access: Exit 201, then south and west on Corn Springs Rd: about 7-8 mi of compacted/graded dirt with soft sandy wash crossings (a 2019 review said '4WD recommended'), climbing gently to about 1,600 ft. Condition after the October 2026 storm is unknown.
camps.priceTent: $6/night, first come first served, 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: First come, first served: 9 sites including 1 group site, no reservations. Quiet hours 9pm-8am.
camps.cyclistNotes: A palm oasis with petroglyphs, shade ramadas, tables and grills; usually nearly empty midweek. BLM lists potable water, but a Jan 30, 2026 visitor reported 'No water available', so carry all you need. The round trip is more than 15 mi of dirt and sand. The Countri Bike rider (2016-17) considered it and went on to Chiriaco.

camps.name: Lake Tamarisk Desert Resort (no tents)
camps.access: Paved: exit 192, then 2 mi north on Rice Rd (CA 177) and Parkview Dr.
camps.priceTent: Tents not allowed. Park rules: 'Only one RV per site - everyone must sleep in the RV; no tent camping' and 'Tents and outdoor sleeping is not permitted.' RV sites start at $50/night including electricity.
camps.reservations: RoverPass online or phone. Check-in is at 1 pm; register at the office.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only campground at Desert Center, and it bans tents. It is a 55+ park, and RVs must be 15 years old or newer. The county library next door has water Tue/Thu 10-6 and Sat 10-2.

camps.name: BLM land south of Desert Center, I-10 exit 192
camps.address: South side of I-10 exit 192, Desert Center, CA 92239
camps.access: Exit 192 (Desert Center). On the south side a rough dirt track (OSM grade 4) runs south-west across BLM land; camp a few hundred yards in. Off limits: the town lots, the Caltrans yard, and the fenced Oberon/Athos solar fields north and east of the exit.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map). Halfway between Blythe and Chiriaco. Desert Center has NO store, water or gas, so carry dinner, breakfast and water for the 19 mi to Chiriaco. Lake Tamarisk Library, 2 mi north, has a fountain only Tue/Thu/Sat in the daytime.

camps.name: BLM land north of Eagle Mountain Rd, I-10 exit 189
camps.address: Eagle Mountain Rd at I-10 exit 189, 3 mi west of Desert Center
camps.access: Exit 189, then north on paved Eagle Mountain Rd. BLM desert lies on both sides just north of the interchange.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map; no solar fields mapped here). An alternative to the Desert Center exit. Dry camp.

camps.name: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM)
camps.address: Red Cloud Mine Rd at I-10 exit 182, Desert Center, CA 92239
camps.access: Exit 182 (Red Cloud Rd), south side. A big gravel lot sits right by I-10, and dispersed sites run along a 2.2-mi graded dirt road toward the Chuckwalla Mtns. Light washboard and dips, with soft sand in places: a 2WD van got stuck in 2022.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only DOCUMENTED dispersed area near the line between Blythe and Chiriaco (Campendium, 6 reviews, latest Apr 2023). Freeway noise near the lot, a high-voltage line nearby, Border Patrol around. It is 9.5 mi before the Chiriaco store, which makes it the stop if daylight runs out (sunset is about 4:45 pm PST). No water.

camps.name: Chiriaco Summit - Patton Museum Dry Camp Area
camps.address: Behind the General Patton Memorial Museum, 62450 Chiriaco Rd, Chiriaco Summit, CA 92201
camps.access: Exit 173. Paved to the museum, then take the dirt access road on the right side of the museum (sign: 'Welcome to Chiriaco Summit Dry Camp Area') to marked sites behind it. About 0.3 mi; the Chevron and cafe are about 400 m away.
camps.priceTent: Free. There are no facilities at the sites; water and restrooms are at the Chevron food mart (open 24 h) and the coffee shop, 400 m away.
camps.reservations: First come, first served. A camp host takes your name and plate number. If you arrive after dark, set up and check in the next morning (Dec 2024 review). Maximum stay is 5-7 nights.
camps.cyclistNotes: The key camp on this segment: free, hosted, on BLM land, with marked sites including tent-only spots and stone fire rings. The NPS lists Chiriaco Summit as a camping option south of the park. Nearby: the Chevron food mart (24 h), Foster's Freeze (8am-9pm) and the coffee shop (6am-11pm). A 2021 reviewer got free water at the station. Some I-10 truck noise. A cyclist camped here in 2016 and sat in the coffee shop until it closed. A Jan 2026 reviewer described a dozen trucks parked in the area, so confirm with the host or the store. It is 68 mi from Blythe and 49 mi from the last water at Wiley's Well.

camps.name: Joshua Tree South BLM Dispersed Camping (Cottonwood Springs Rd)
camps.address: Cottonwood Springs Rd at I-10 exit 168 (north side), 4 mi west of Chiriaco Summit
camps.access: Exit 168, then north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd; dirt roads branch east and west just north of the freeway and are passable by car. Camp only in the BLM sections on the NPS map: east of the road between I-10 and the Edison power-line road, west of the road north of the power line, and a block further east. It is checkerboarded with private land, and the NPS says to camp 300+ ft from roadways.
camps.priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
camps.reservations: None, first come. There are hundreds of fire-ring sites and it effectively never fills.
camps.cyclistNotes: 155 Campendium reviews through May 2026; a 2024 tent camper liked it, and the NPS BLM map was updated May 2026. The ground is crushed granite and sand, with little freeway noise. Mostly RVs, busier on weekends; good Verizon/T-Mobile coverage. No water: fill at Chiriaco, 4.3 mi east, or at Cottonwood, 6 mi uphill (needs the $15 park entry). This is also mile ~4 of the Mecca variant.

camps.name: Cottonwood Campground (Joshua Tree National Park)
camps.address: Pinto Basin Rd by the Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree National Park
camps.access: Exit 168, then 7 mi north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd/Pinto Basin Rd, climbing about 1,250 ft (1,750 to 3,000 ft). Slow when loaded; return the same way. The NPS describes the park's paved roads as crumbling and uneven.
camps.priceTent: $35/site/night (up to 6 people and 3 tents), plus a $15 per-person 7-day park entry on a bike. Group tent-only sites cost $55.
camps.reservations: Reservation only, year-round, on recreation.gov. There is NO cell service at the campground, so book before leaving I-10. Check-in at noon; the campground is open 24 h. Availability on the night of Nov 1: 43-50 sites free for Mon-Thu Nov 2-5 and Mon Nov 9, 26 for Sun Nov 8, but only 1 site (B16) left for each of Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only campground with potable water and flush toilets between Blythe and Indio; no showers. Limit is 14 nights Oct-May. A riding group in Dec 2019 found it full, and rangers enforced the rules. The only current park alert is the Geology Tour Rd flood closure, which is not on this route. Worth the climb only for water and a proper site.

camps.name: Box Canyon Rd / Mecca Hills BLM dispersed camping (ROAD CLOSED)
camps.address: Box Canyon Rd (old SR 195) through the Mecca Hills, between I-10 exit 168 and Mecca
camps.access: CLOSED. A BLM notice dated Oct 21, 2026, still posted Nov 1, says: 'Box Canyon Road is closed from Pinto Road to Painted Canyon Road due to flooding damage from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel'; follow the Riverside County closure signs. When open, the road is paved and descends gently, with BLM land at variant miles ~12-19. My reading is that the 5.8 mi between Mecca and Painted Canyon Rd lie outside the closure; that is an inference, not stated.
camps.priceTent: Free (when the road is open).
camps.reservations: None.
camps.cyclistNotes: Cyclists wild-camped in the canyon in Oct 2023 (on a closed road) and Mar 2024. Camp only in the non-wilderness road corridor: bikes are banned in the Mecca Hills Wilderness on both sides. Never camp in a wash bottom, and expect wind to blow sand into the tent. Near the canyon mouth (variant mile ~20) the land is tribal (BIA), where you cannot camp.

camps.name: Salton Sea SRA - Headquarters / New Camp (hike-and-bike sites)
camps.access: Paved and flat, at -230 ft. From Mecca take 66th Ave/Lincoln St to Hwy 111 south, about 11.6 mi each way; a 2016 rider reported a wide, clean shoulder. This is on the hybrid line's CA 111 route.
camps.priceTent: Developed tent site $20/night; primitive $10; hookup $30. Hike-and-bike sites are listed but no fee is posted; in 2016 the host told a cyclist to take any site.
camps.reservations: ReserveCalifornia Oct-May; on Nov 1 it showed availability for every start date Nov 4-16. The campground is open 24 h; the visitor center 9-4.
camps.cyclistNotes: CA State Parks restrictions (checked 11/1/2026) say the main campground is open; Mecca Beach and Bombay Beach are closed. Showers and potable water are mapped at New Camp. Freight trains beside Hwy 111 run all night. It is 12 mi off the variant each way, so it only makes sense on the hybrid's Salton Sea line.

camps.name: Mecca Beach Campground, Salton Sea SRA (CLOSED)
camps.address: Hwy 111, Salton Sea SRA, Mecca, CA 92254
camps.access: Paved, 12.4 mi south of Mecca on Hwy 111.
camps.priceTent: $20 developed tent site when open.
camps.reservations: Closed.
camps.cyclistNotes: CLOSED. CA State Parks (checked 11/1/2026): 'Mecca Beach Campground is currently closed for maintenance repairs. It is unknown when the campground will reopen.' Use the Headquarters campground 0.8 mi north.

camps.name: Oasis Palms RV Resort
camps.access: Paved and flat, about 10.4 mi south of Mecca toward the north-west shore of the Salton Sea.
camps.priceTent: $55/night 'Grass/Tent Site', including water, electricity, sewer and Wi-Fi for up to 4 adults; $320 weekly.
camps.reservations: Phone or email (OasisRVResorthelp@gmail.com). Bookings are usually taken up to a month ahead. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am; register at the front office.
camps.cyclistNotes: The website sells grass/tent sites outright, and a 2016 cyclist had tents confirmed by email. It has a pool, spa, laundry, showers and drinking-water stations (use those rather than the site taps), and a gas station within walking distance. OSM lists an older phone, +1 760-397-1011. Too far off the variant unless you are already routing via the Salton Sea.

camps.name: Lake Cahuilla Veterans Regional Park (Riverside County)
camps.access: Paved and flat. About 10 mi south-west of central Indio by the bike router (Jackson/Monroe/Jefferson St to Avenue 58), or about 9.4 mi from the Mecca variant near Thermal (variant mile ~33). Over 10 mi, but there is no closer public campground in Indio.
camps.priceTent: Unknown for 2026. Primitive/dry sites were about $20 in 2023; an Apr 2026 review put hookup sites at about $45 on weeknights and $75 Fri-Sun. Showers take a few quarters.
camps.reservations: Riverside County Parks online reservations or phone. Rarely full midweek. 14-night max. Late-arrival rules unknown.
camps.cyclistNotes: A proper campground with hot coin showers and a seasonal pool. Primitive sites sit on the concrete-lined reservoir (no swimming). The sheriff's gun range across the lake is loud by day, and it gets dusty in wind. The latest review (Apr 2026) is positive. A ~20-mi round trip, so best for a rest/shower day.

camps.name: Shadow Hills RV Resort
camps.access: Paved: from the line on Indio Blvd at Jefferson St, 1.2 mi north on Jefferson St across I-10. Just past this segment's end; the first tent option west of central Indio.
camps.priceTent: Unknown. The 'Desert Glamping Oasis' tent spaces (about 10x20 ft, each with a power outlet and fresh water) are not priced online; RV sites were about $65/night in June 2026.
camps.reservations: Online (Newbook) or by phone. After-hours check-in packets are left for late arrivals (2024 review). Gated. No refund for cancellations within 29 days.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only Indio RV resort that advertises tent spaces ('tent sites, RV sites, and cabins' in its FAQ), each with its own outlet. It has a pool, laundry and a duck pond, and is clean and strictly run. Some freeway noise. Call to confirm tent spaces are sold outside festival season.

camps.name: Forsythe Equestrian Club (Hipcamp)
camps.address: Vista Santa Rosa, south of Indio (exact address shared after booking)
camps.access: Paved and flat: about 5.7 mi south of central Indio, or 7 mi from the Dillon Rd exit. The coordinates are Hipcamp's approximate pin.
camps.priceTent: About $75/night, the minimum price on the listing; check the per-site price on Hipcamp.
camps.reservations: Book on Hipcamp; some sites are instant-book; check-in is on arrival.
camps.cyclistNotes: A horse property with 2 'RV/tent' sites listing a toilet and a water hookup ('No potable water'); the separate on-site RV rental has a shower. Rated 4.65. Pricey for a tent, but legal and close to Indio if Shadow Hills is full.

camps.name: Coachella Lakes RV Resort (no tents)
camps.access: Paved, 0.9 mi from the Dillon Rd exit (146), where bikes must leave I-10.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites: Campspot shows 0 tent sites, with RV sites from $90/night. Campendium's 'tent camping: yes' tag is wrong.
camps.reservations: Campspot.
camps.cyclistNotes: Right at the bike exit, but it rents only RV sites and cottages.

camps.name: Indian Wells Sun RV Community (no tents)
camps.access: Paved, 3.9 mi from central Indio.
camps.priceTent: No tenting (2021 reviewer: 'one of the reasons for no tenting allowed'). RV sites were about $119/night in Feb 2025.
camps.reservations: Sun Outdoors online.
camps.cyclistNotes: RV-only; not a tent option.

camps.name: Outdoor Resort Indio (no tents)
camps.access: Paved, about 3 mi south of the line in Indio.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites. It is an owner-occupied motorcoach resort that rents owners' lots through the office (about $100/night in 2023).
camps.reservations: Through the resort office.
camps.cyclistNotes: A luxury motorcoach/owner community; not a tent option.

camps.name: Motorcoach Country Club (no tents)
camps.access: Paved, about 3 mi south of the line in Indio.
camps.priceTent: No tent sites; motorcoach-only luxury resort, about $99/night in 2021.
camps.reservations: Through the resort.
camps.cyclistNotes: Not a tent option. The nearby Desert Shores and Rancho Casa Blanca are owner-lot communities (Class A-only and park models) with no overnight tent use.

research.waterAndFood:
Stock up in Blythe (mi ~196-198), which has full services. Bikes must ride Hobsonway/Chanslor Way west through town; the last store is BB Travel Center/Chevron at the Mesa Dr on-ramp, exit 232 (mi ~206, 24 h, 760-922-5109).

Wiley's Well Rest Area (exit 222, mi ~216) has 24-h taps and restrooms; the well water is mineral-heavy, and Caltrans has filed for a water/wastewater rebuild with no dates.

Then nothing on the line for 49 mi:
- Desert Center (mi 246) has no store, gas or cafe. The cafe closed in 2012, and in 2023 the post office awning was the only working building.
- Lake Tamarisk Library, 1.8 mi north of exit 192, has a fountain Tue/Thu 10-6 and Sat 10-2 only.
- Corn Springs campground's tap was dry in Jan 2026.

Chiriaco Summit (mi 265.5):
- Chevron food mart open 24 h, Foster's Freeze 8am-9pm, coffee shop/restaurant 6am-11pm (operator site).
- A 2021 visitor got free water at the station.
- Patton Museum open 9:30-4:30.

Joshua Tree's Cottonwood campground/visitor center, 7 mi uphill from exit 168, has potable water ($15 park entry on a bike).

The Cactus City rest areas (mi ~279) are CLOSED for reconstruction until spring 2027. So Chiriaco to the Dillon Rd truck stops (exit 146, mi ~292: Love's and TA 24 h, Chevron, Santiago's 24/7, fast food) is 26.5 mi with no water. Indio has full services.

Mecca variant: Chiriaco to Mecca is 24.7 mi with no services, and Box Canyon Rd is closed. Mecca has the Spirit station on Hammond Rd, ARCO ampm/Subway at 66th Ave and Hwy 111, and taquerias. There is a Sinclair in Thermal, and Coachella's Food 4 Less/Cardenas are near CV Link.

LONGEST STRETCHES:
- No water from Wiley's Well RA to Chiriaco, about 49.5 mi.
- No food from exit 232 to Chiriaco, about 59 mi.

Leave Blythe with 5-6 L. Dry-camping anywhere between exits 222 and 182 needs about 3 L more, plus dinner and breakfast. (Store hours beyond the operator site come from this run's services research.)
research.legality:
BIKES ON I-10
- OSM tags, which mirror Caltrans signs, show bicycle=no on I-10 through Blythe (east of town to Mesa Dr, exit 232) and west of Dillon Rd (exit 146).
- Bicycles are allowed between those points, and on the Colorado River bridge, which is part of USBR 90 with a wide shoulder.
- So ride Hobsonway/Chanslor Way through Blythe, enter I-10 westbound at exit 232, and leave at exit 146 for Dillon Rd/CV Link into Indio. The app's regenerated I-10 line already does this.

ROAD CONDITIONS
- Riders report a shoulder 8-10 ft wide beyond a rumble strip, with debris and steel wire from shredded truck tires. Expect flats: run sealant and carry 3+ tubes.
- Riders also report heat cracks for about 20 mi east of Indio, drifted sand, and 70+ mph trucks.
- Caltrans highway info (Nov 1, 9:14 PM) shows no restrictions on I-10 between Blythe and Indio.
- Caltrans is rebuilding the Cactus City rest areas (mi ~279). Both are closed until spring 2027. Day work runs M-F 6am-3pm, with possible alternating lane closures at night and on weekends, so expect cones and a narrowed shoulder.

STORM DAMAGE (Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, Oct 2026)
- Box Canyon Rd, the Mecca variant, has been CLOSED from Pinto Rd at I-10 to Painted Canyon Rd since Oct 21 (BLM notice, still posted Nov 1). Riding it means passing county closure signs.
- Wiley's Well Rd (LTVA access) is damaged and 4x4-only (Oct 15).
- Joshua Tree's Geology Tour Rd is closed for flooding (not on route).

CAMPING RULES
- BLM land, much of it now Chuckwalla National Monument, allows free dispersed camping for up to 14 days unless posted.
- At exit 168 the NPS says to camp only in the BLM sections on its map (checkerboarded with private land) and 300+ ft from roadways.
- Midland LTVA bans camping that is not self-contained, so no tents.
- Mule Mountain LTVA allows tents only at designated Wiley's Well/Coon Hollow sites within 500 ft of a vault toilet, with a $40 short-visit permit (Sept 15-Apr 15).
- Caltrans rest areas: 8-hour limit, no tents.
- Joshua Tree NP: camping only in campgrounds; roadside sleeping is cited.
- Lake Tamarisk Desert Resort (Desert Center) prohibits tents and outdoor sleeping.
- Casinos (Fantasy Springs, Spotlight 29) allow RV/vehicle overnight parking with a security pass, not tents.
research.gapWarnings:
1) MAIN LINE, Blythe to Red Cloud Mine Rd (mi ~197 to 256, about 59 mi): no DOCUMENTED tent site within 1 mi of the line.
- Blythe's tent sites (Mayflower, McIntyre) are 7-8 mi off. The Cove (0.5 mi off at mi 193.5) has not confirmed tents.
- Documented detours: Wiley's Well campground (exit 222, 9 mi south on storm-damaged dirt, $40 LTVA permit, no water) and Corn Springs campground (exit 201, about 7.8 mi on sandy dirt, $6, tap dry in Jan 2026).
- Legal but undocumented BLM fallbacks right at the exits, all dry camps: 222 (mi 216, with water and toilets at the rest area, the best of them), 201 (mi 236.5), 192 Desert Center (mi 246), 189 (mi 249.4).
- Desert Center's only campground (Lake Tamarisk) bans tents, and the town has no services.
- Realistic plan: a Blythe RV park, then Chiriaco dry camp or JT South BLM (68-73 mi from Blythe).
- On a 50-mi wind day, stop at Red Cloud Mine Rd (59 mi) or a Desert Center/Eagle Mtn BLM spot (49-52 mi), carrying water.
- Forecast for Nov 6-8: N crosswinds 8-14 mph, gusts 17-25, at Desert Center and Chiriaco. Sunset is about 4:45 pm PST (DST ended Nov 1).

2) Chiriaco/JT South (mi 265.5-270) to Indio, about 26-30 mi, is OK.
- There is no legal camp on I-10 between exit 168 and Indio.
- The tent options are Forsythe Hipcamp (5.7 mi off), Shadow Hills (1.2 mi off at mi ~299, just past the segment end) and Lake Cahuilla (10 mi off).
- The RV resorts nearest the line do NOT take tents: Coachella Lakes at the bike exit, Indian Wells Sun, Outdoor Resort Indio, Motorcoach CC, Desert Shores, Rancho Casa Blanca.
- Casino lots (Fantasy Springs, Spotlight 29) are for RVs and vehicles only.
- Cottonwood campground has only 1 site left for Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.

3) MECCA VARIANT: Box Canyon Rd is closed, so its BLM camping (variant mi ~12-19) and the road itself are off limits.
- From JT South (variant mi ~4) to Indio (41.5) there is no camp on the line.
- Nearest off-line: Lake Cahuilla (9.4 mi from variant mi 33), Oasis Palms RV (10.4 mi south of Mecca, $55 tent), Salton Sea SRA HQ (11.6 mi south of Mecca).
- Treat the variant as unavailable until Riverside County reopens Box Canyon Rd.

4) Just east of the segment, Ehrenberg (AZ) BLM dispersed camping (Ehrenberg-Cibola Rd/Levee Rd) belongs to the Quartzsite-Blythe segment.

5) Mile numbers follow this task's anchors (Blythe 197.4, Desert Center 246.3, Chiriaco 265.5, Indio 295.8). The app's lines.json was regenerated at 22:17 (Blythe 212.1, Mesa Dr 220.9, Desert Center 269.2, Chiriaco 288.4, Dillon Rd 314.9, Indio 319.1); re-project from lat/lng.

camps.name: Shadow Hills RV Resort (Desert Glamping Oasis tent spaces)
camps.access: Paved and flat. About 0.4 mi off the line where it crosses Jefferson St in north Indio, just south of I-10. Gated resort.
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not published. The Dyrt shows rates from $42/night, which is probably the tent space but that is not confirmed. RV sites run about $65 (Campendium, Jun 2026). Tent spaces are about 10x20 ft with an outdoor power outlet and fresh water, plus use of the resort (heated pool, hot tub, showers, laundry).
camps.reservations: Book online with the resort's 'Book Now' button (Newbook) or by phone or office@shadowhillsrvresort.com. Office hours and late-arrival rules are not published, so call ahead. Bookings cancelled 29 days or less before arrival are not refunded.
camps.cyclistNotes: The best tent spot in the Coachella Valley: the operator's 'Ways to Stay' page and FAQ both list tent sites ('Desert Glamping Oasis' spaces by the ponds and walking trail), and tent guests get full use of the resort. It sits right on the line at the east end of the valley. Reviews mention some noise from the local road and the freeway. Good last night before the 30-mi stretch through Palm Desert and Palm Springs, where there is no on-line campground confirmed to take tents.

camps.name: Lake Cahuilla Veterans Regional Park campground (Riverside County)
camps.access: Paved and flat. About 10 mi south of the line in Indio via Jackson/Monroe St, Ave 54, Madison St and Ave 58 (bike router). Riding straight down Jefferson St from where the line crosses it is about 11.5 mi. It is a dead end, so you ride the same way back.
camps.priceTent: Primitive (no hookup) tent sites were $25 in 2022 and were first come, first served then. A partial hookup was about $30 in 2022 (needed for power). An Apr 2026 reviewer paid $45 on weeknights and $75 Fri-Sun for a hookup site. Online booking adds about $8. Pets $4. Showers are coin-op.
camps.reservations: Book online through Riverside County Parks or by phone. Dry and primitive sites sold out during a fishing-derby weekend in Nov 2025, so book or arrive midweek. Gate and office hours not confirmed (the county website blocks automated reading).
camps.cyclistNotes: County park on a concrete-lined fishing reservoir under the Santa Rosa Mtns, open year round. It has a tent/primitive section by the lake and big gravel pads with little shade. The bathhouse is older but clean (a reviewer counted 3 stalls and 2 showers). Gunfire from a range across the lake until dark and early truck noise on the access road have been reported. Worth it only if Shadow Hills is full, because it costs about 20 mi out and back.

camps.name: Forsythe Equestrian Club (Hipcamp)
camps.access: Paved and flat. About 6.3 mi south of the line in Indio via Jackson St, Monroe St and Ave 54 to Vista Santa Rosa (bike router). The exact address comes after booking.
camps.address: Vista Santa Rosa, south of Indio/Coachella (exact address after booking)
camps.priceTent: $75/night for the site, $88.30 with Hipcamp fees. Tent or RV site with 30A power, water and septic hookups.
camps.reservations: Hipcamp Instant Book. A 3-night minimum applies only on the Apr 2027 Coachella festival weekends.
camps.cyclistNotes: A 20-acre horse property 2.7 mi from the Coachella festival grounds, quiet at night. Expensive for one tent, but it is instant-book with showers and power. 93% recommend (20 ratings, 39 bookings).

camps.name: Thousand Trails Palm Springs RV Resort
camps.access: Paved and flat. On Varner Rd just north of I-10 at Washington St, about 0.5 mi off the line.
camps.priceTent: No tent site type is offered. Non-member RV sites were about $46/night (Campendium, Dec 2025). WiFi costs extra.
camps.reservations: Non-members can book nightly online. Campsite check-in is at noon; the office is open Mon-Fri 9-5. A reviewer advises arriving in daylight.
camps.cyclistNotes: Open for the season 9/15/2026-5/15/2027. Its rules allow '1 RV, 2 vehicles, and 2 tents' per site, but booking only offers RV back-in and pull-through sites. Call and ask whether a tent-only cyclist can take an RV site. It has a pool, spa, showers and laundry, and sits right on the line.

camps.name: Indian Wells RV Resort (Sun Outdoors 'Indian Wells RV Community')
camps.access: Paved and flat. About 3 mi south of the line on Jefferson St, south of Hwy 111.
camps.priceTent: unknown
camps.reservations: unknown (the operator site blocks automated reading)
camps.cyclistNotes: Now branded as an 'RV community', which suggests long-stay guests. The Dyrt lists tent sites, but it has no reviews and that tag is generic. Call before counting on it; Shadow Hills is closer and confirmed.

camps.name: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp)
camps.access: About 9.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Long Canyon Rd/21st Ave (bike router). The last mile is a maintained dirt road. About 200-250 ft of net climbing (to about 770 ft). The host sends directions because phone GPS is often wrong.
camps.address: 21st Ave area between Palm Springs and Desert Hot Springs (exact address after booking)
camps.priceTent: $39/night, $45.93 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Under Desert Skies' tent/RV site with power and water hookups.
camps.reservations: Request to book (not instant). The host approves, then emails registration and waiver forms, and gives a 15-minute orientation on arrival. Full refund if you cancel 3 or more days ahead. Request at least a day or two before you arrive.
camps.cyclistNotes: The closest good tent spot to Palm Springs: hot outdoor showers, accessible porta-potties, mineral well water and an outdoor kitchen. 575 bookings, 97% recommend. The host warns of frequent high winds and near-freezing winter nights. The pool is winterized mid-Oct to April. It is a sober community farm.

camps.name: Palm Springs / Joshua Tree KOA
camps.access: About 11.7 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave and Mountain View Rd to Dillon Rd (bike router). The router uses some minor desert roads, and Dillon Rd is the paved fallback. You climb about 500 ft, to roughly 1,040 ft.
camps.address: 70405 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241
camps.priceTent: Tent rate not found (the KOA site blocks automated reading). A 2021 tent camper called the price 'a bit much'. RV sites ran about $91 (Jun 2025).
camps.reservations: Book with KOA online or by phone. Office hours and after-hours check-in not confirmed; staff escort guests to sites.
camps.cyclistNotes: The only conventional tent campground between Indio and Whitewater: a 287-site resort with a separate tent area (sinks shared), keypad bathhouses with private showers, a hot-spring pool and hot tub, a store and coin laundry. A Mar 2025 review mentions strong wind hitting tents. Reviews run through Mar 2026. The detour is about 23 mi round trip, so treat it as a fallback.

camps.name: Joshua Tree, Palm Springs, Coachella Adjacent (private campground, The Dyrt)
camps.access: About 11.1 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and minor roads near Corkill Rd (bike router). The last roads may be sandy. Climb of about 450 ft.
camps.address: Desert Hot Springs, Dillon Rd/Corkill Rd area (exact address on booking)
camps.priceTent: $15-25/night (The Dyrt listing).

camps.name: Catalina Spa & RV Resort

camps.name: Sam's Family Spa Hot Water Resort

camps.name: Windy Point x Palm Springs (Hipcamp off-grid lot)

The host warns that 'Standard free-standing tents generally don't work here' because gusts can reach gale force. Book it only when the forecast is light, and read the host's wind report. camps.name: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy)
camps.access: Paved. Leave CA-111 at Tipton Rd and follow Whitewater Cutoff to Whitewater Canyon Rd at Bonnie Bell, then 4.2 mi up the 2-lane canyon road to the preserve. camps.priceTent: Free (donations appreciated).
camps.reservations: Reserve at least 48 h ahead with the online request form (check the campground calendar first). Walk-ins are accepted only if the campground is not full and you check in at the ranger station before 4:15 pm. The preserve is open 8 am-5 pm. Check-out 11 am. Up to 3 nights per 30 days; capacity 30 guests a day. Reservations can be cancelled for hazardous weather.
camps.cyclistNotes: The best-value stop on the segment: a free tent area with flush toilets, drinking water, a river and ponds. No fires of any kind, no generators, and no cell signal on site (signal starts about 3.5 mi down the road). The WHOLE PRESERVE WAS CLOSED SUN 11/1/2026 for hazardous weather and flood conditions, and the operator warns of more El Nino closures this winter. Confirm with whitewaterpreserve@wildlandsconservancy.org or by phone, and submit the form by about Nov 3 for a Nov 5-6 night. If you miss the 4:15 pm check-in, fall back to the Windy Point lot or to Banning KOA (about 15 mi on, with after-hours self check-in).

The monument page sends campers to BLM's general dispersed-camping rules but says nothing about this canyon, and no camper or rider report was found. Last resort only, for example if you miss the preserve's 4:15 pm check-in. Stay out of sight of homes and make no fire. The pass mouth is very windy.

research.waterAndFood:
Water and food are easy except in the pass.

Indio through Palm Desert, Rancho Mirage, Cathedral City and Palm Springs (mi ~292-322) has continuous services:
- Dillon Rd truck stops (Love's/TA, 24 h) at mi ~292.
- Groceries in Indio on Jackson St and Hwy 111 (WinCo, Food 4 Less, Cardenas, Walmart).
- Shopping every 1-2 mi on Country Club Dr, and drinking fountains on CV Link.

The last on-route stops in Palm Springs are a 7-Eleven, Del Taco and Carl's Jr. (mi ~321.2) and a Shell with Larry's Deli (mi ~321.7).

Through the pass:
- Windy Cove Market & Gas (Pemex), 60490 Overture Dr near the CA-111/I-10 junction (mi ~325.5), is the only shop in the Windy Point hamlet.
- Whitewater rest area on I-10 (mi ~331, both directions): water and restrooms, no vending. The line rides the I-10 shoulder there.
- Whitewater Preserve, 7-9 mi off route, has potable water.

Cabazon from mi ~338.4: Shell, Gulf, Burger King, Dollar General, Circle K, 76, In-N-Out, Ruby's Diner, McDonald's and Chevron, plus the Morongo Casino and the outlets. Banning (Ramsey St: Arco 24/7, Chevron, Banning Village Market) and Beaumont have continuous services.

Longest stretch without a store is about 13 mi, Windy Cove Market to Cabazon (16.7 mi from the last Palm Springs Shell), with the rest area in between for water. Longest stretch without any water is about 6-7 mi, rest area to Cabazon. Carry 2-3 L for the roughly 1,300-ft climb from Palm Springs (about 500 ft) to Cabazon (about 1,820 ft). It continues to about 2,600 ft at Beaumont.

The Windy Point Hipcamp and the BLM canyon land have no water; the Desert Hot Springs Hipcamps and KOA do.

research.legality:
Bike access on I-10, from the Caltrans District 8 bike-access GIS layer (services1.arcgis.com/8CpMUd3fdw6aXef7 'D8_bike_map_web' FeatureServer/0, last edited 2021):

1. OPEN on the shoulder from Dillon Rd (Coachella, exit 146) east to Mesa Dr in Blythe.
2. CLOSED from Dillon Rd west to the SR-62 junction, which is the whole Coachella Valley. The line uses Indio Blvd, Country Club Dr, CV Link and CA-111 instead.
3. OPEN for about 4.7 mi between the SR-62 junction and Haugen-Lehmann Way at Whitewater. The current line rides CA-111 to its I-10 junction, then the I-10 shoulder to Haugen-Lehmann Way. This is also the legal way back west after a night at Whitewater Preserve: rejoin at the Whitewater exit.
4. CLOSED from Haugen-Lehmann Way west to the LA/San Bernardino county line. Cabazon to Banning to Beaumont must be on surface roads: Johnson Lane (asphalt, along the railroad north of I-10), then Ramsey St / US 99 Hist.

Morongo Reservation, between Cabazon and Banning: the roads cross Morongo Reservation (BIA trust) land.
- In 2024 an eastbound rider (Nick Sanders) was turned away at a reservation gate when his GPS routed him onto tribal roads. A local sent him along the railroad road instead.
- A 2023 supported tour needed a police escort through the reservation.
- A 2018 tour rode about 2 mi of I-10 through Cabazon, which D8 lists as closed to bikes.
- Stick to the line (Johnson Ln / Ramsey St) and don't follow phone GPS onto gated tribal roads.

Road notes:
- Whitewater Canyon Rd is a 2-lane paved county road (OSM), climbing about 1,000 ft to the preserve. Reach it from CA-111 by Tipton Rd and Whitewater Cutoff.
- Expect wire from shredded truck tires on any I-10 shoulder; every recent I-10 report mentions flats.
- Palm Springs traffic is heavy, with many junctions (2023 report).

Wind: the pass mouth (Windy Point, CA-111/I-10, the Whitewater wind farms) is where the wind blows. In an average November it blows 20-35 mph from the west about 3 days in 10. For Nov 5-8, 2026 NWS shows easterly flow, a tailwind for a westbound rider, strongest at dawn.

The Windy Point Hipcamp host warns free-standing tents often fail there.
research.gapWarnings:
No stretch of this segment goes more than 30 mi without a tent-legal option, if Hipcamp and The Dyrt private sites count.

Confirmed tent spots by corridor mile (riding miles off route in brackets):
- 295.8: Forsythe Equestrian Club Hipcamp [6]
- 295.8: Lake Cahuilla county park [10]
- 299.8: Shadow Hills RV Resort [0.5]
- 321: DragonflyHill Hipcamp [9.6]
- 321: Desert Hot Springs / Dillon Rd cluster [11-14]: Palm Springs/Joshua Tree KOA, 'Joshua Tree, Palm Springs, Coachella Adjacent', Rancho Capotista, Relaxing Hide Away, Scorpion Ranch
- 327: Windy Point Hipcamp lot [0.6]
- 329.6: Whitewater Preserve [7-9.5]
- 345.1: Banning Stagecoach KOA [1]
- 353.7: Bogart Regional Park [2.3]

WEAKEST STRETCH: Shadow Hills (299.8) to Whitewater Preserve (329.6) is about 30 mi through Palm Desert, Rancho Mirage, Cathedral City and Palm Springs with no on-line campground confirmed to take tents.
- On-line fallbacks: the off-grid Windy Point lot (no water or toilet; the host says free-standing tents fail in wind), or call-first RV parks: Thousand Trails 302.2, Palm Springs Oasis 311.8, Happy Traveler 318.3.
- Everything else needs a 10-14 mi, 400-800 ft climb north to the Desert Hot Springs cluster.
- If the preserve is closed or full, the realistic plan is Indio/Shadow Hills to Banning KOA: about 45 mi and about 2,300 ft of climbing.

TIMING TRAPS:
- Whitewater Preserve (free) needs the online form at least 48 h ahead, or a walk-in check-in before 4:15 pm. It was CLOSED 11/1/2026 for flood conditions, so confirm it has reopened.
- Bogart books only by phone during office hours (Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-noon). It has no weekday attendant, and the gate may be shut in the evening.
- DragonflyHill is request-to-book, so allow a day for host approval.
- Banning KOA has after-hours self check-in, which makes it the safest late arrival in the pass.

NOT OPTIONS:
- Morongo Casino: overnight RV parking ended in 2025, and there is no camping.
- Whitewater rest area: not a campground.
- Spotlight 29 Casino (mi ~292.6, just east): RV overnight lot only.
- Tents banned, Class A only or self-contained only: Emerald Desert, Indian Waters, Outdoor Resort Indio, Motorcoach Country Club, Desert Shores, Outdoor Resort Palm Springs, Sky Valley.
- 55+ only: Caliente Springs and Sands RV & Golf.
- Residential park-model or trailer communities, not campgrounds: Rancho Casa Blanca, Sky Ridge, Date Palm Country Club.
- Mountain campgrounds, 11+ mi straight-line and 3,000-5,000 ft above the line: Idyllwild / Mt San Jacinto SP (including its hike-and-bike site), Black Mountain, Boulder Basin, and Round Valley via the tram.
- Wandering Caboose Ranch (The Dyrt): up Twin Pines Rd, about 15 mi and about 1,800 ft above Banning. Excluded.

BEYOND THE SEGMENT END: the next tent options are Yucaipa Regional Park and Cherry Valley Lakes (membership), in the next segment.

RESEARCH LIMITS: the web-search budget was used up before this agent started, so this list was built from operator sites, Hipcamp, The Dyrt and Campendium town and nearby listings, OSM/Nominatim, the BLM land-status map, Caltrans GIS and the bike router. rivcoparks.org and koa.com blocked automated reading, so the Lake Cahuilla and KOA tent prices are unconfirmed.

MILES: corridor miles use this task's anchors: Indio 295.8, Palm Springs 319.6, Cabazon 339.3, Banning 345.1, Beaumont 350.9. data/corridors/lines.json was regenerated twice during this run. In the latest version Indio is 306.7 and Beaumont 359.6, and Palm Springs to Cabazon is now 17.5 mi by CA-111 and I-10. Treat lat/lng as authoritative.

research.waterAndFood:
Urban almost the whole way. OpenStreetMap shows about 1,000 stores, fuel stations and eateries within 0.35 mi of the line from Beaumont to the Elysian Theater, plus about 59 mapped drinking fountains (parks and the Pacific Electric Trail).

Longest stretches with no food or store on the line:
- 4.6 mi, mile 352.3–357.0: Beaumont Ave/Cherry Valley Blvd to the Calimesa Starbucks/Chevron at I-10.
- 4.2 mi, mile 360.2–364.3: Calimesa Blvd–Dunlap Blvd into south Redlands.
- Everywhere else, under 3.1 mi.

Camps without drinking water:
- Gould Mesa: creek only, treat it. Fill bottles in Pasadena or La Cañada before the trailhead.
- Noble Creek: a 2022 review said it has no restrooms.

The Hipcamps (Riverview Ranch, Harmony Heaven, Unhitched Ranch) list potable water.
research.legality:
Freeways: Caltrans District 8 bicycle-access data shows I-10 is closed to bicycles from the LA/San Bernardino county line east to Haugen-Lehmann Way (Cabazon), which is this whole segment. In LA County, I-10 and I-210 are also closed. The line already uses surface streets only (checked against OSM):
- Hist US 99/6th St into Beaumont, then Beaumont Ave and Cherry Valley Blvd.
- Calimesa Blvd (Hist US 99), then Dunlap Blvd and residential streets (Tennessee St, La Colina Dr, 6th Ave) into Redlands, then Citrus Ave.
- Barton Rd, S E St and W Olive St.
- The Pacific Electric Trail: about 18 mi car-free from Rialto to Claremont, with push-button crossings almost every block. Foothill Blvd/Route 66 runs parallel and is faster.
- Bonita Ave, Juanita Ave, Route 66 (Foothill Blvd/Huntington Dr) and Colorado Blvd.

Access-road cautions:
- Reche Canyon Rd (to Unhitched Ranch) is a narrow two-lane commuter canyon road.
- International Park Rd to Bogart climbs about 450 ft.
- The Gabrielino Trail to Gould Mesa is dirt with creek crossings; bikes are allowed.
- Bike routers suggest the Crafton Hills Ridge Trail near Yucaipa and dirt trails inside Bonelli Park. Stay on pavement with a loaded bike.

Angeles National Forest:
- The Eaton Fire Area Closure (Order 05-01-26-04) runs through Dec 31, 2027. It closes the Mt Wilson Toll Road (including Henninger Flats), the Sam Merrill/Echo Mountain, Mt Lowe and Idlehour trails, and the Millard and Idlehour trail camps.
- Fire danger is 'Very High': no wood fires outside developed sites.
- Dispersed camping elsewhere on the Angeles is legal within stay limits under Order 05-01-24-12, which expires Dec 15, 2026: no more than 3 days a year within 300 ft of a public road, and no more than 7 consecutive days elsewhere.

Park hours and daylight:
- LA County regional parks are closed to day use Mondays and Tuesdays.
- San Bernardino County regional parks keep 7:30 am–5 pm hours from Oct 31, 2026 to May 2027, and close on the third Wednesday of November (Nov 18).
- Daylight saving time ended Nov 1. Sunset is about 4:50–5:00 pm, and most park offices and gates close around then.

Transit: Metro's A Line now runs to Glendora, San Dimas, La Verne and Pomona (opened Sept 19, 2025) and takes bikes. That makes it a legal bail-out from the Bonelli/Fairplex area into LA.
research.gapWarnings:
Overall: no stretch of more than 30 mi on this segment lacks a tent-legal camp. But the gaps between ordinary campgrounds are long, and most need a detour.

1. Yucaipa (mile 360.8) to Bonelli Bluffs (409.1): 48 mi with no public or commercial tent campground within 3 mi of the line. Fillers:
- Unhitched Ranch Hipcamp (372.7): 9 mi off, $100+.
- Rancho Jurupa or Riverview Ranch (382.9): 9 mi off each way, about 16–17 mi extra in total.
- Harmony Heaven Hipcamp safari tent (397.6): 3.5 mi off.
- Fairplex RV Park (408.0): tents not confirmed.
The largest gaps between confirmed camps are Rancho Jurupa to Bonelli (26 mi) and Bonelli to Gould Mesa (25.5 mi).

2. Bonelli Bluffs (409.1) to the Elysian Theater (440.3): 31 mi.
- The only tent-legal site in between is Gould Mesa (434.6). It is primitive (no water, no showers), 6 mi up the Arroyo Seco, and has no page on the new USFS website.
- If Gould Mesa is closed, there is no legal tent camping within about 30 mi of the theater. Millard and Henninger Flats are closed by the Eaton Fire order through 2027.
- For the Nov 9–15 LA stay, the cleanest legal tent base is Bonelli Bluffs ($30) or Fairplex. Commute on the Metro A Line from the San Dimas, La Verne or Pomona stations to Highland Park/Lincoln Heights, then ride about 2–3 mi to the theater.
- Non-tent Hipcamps near the theater:
  - The White Lodge: vintage trailer in Eagle Rock, 0.3 mi off at mile 436.9, about $131–153/night, closed May–Aug.
  - Backyard Glamping SoCal: tiny space in Glendale, about $98.

3. Before the segment: Banning Stagecoach KOA (mile 345.2, covered in I10-E) is 8.5 mi before Bogart.

Checked and excluded:
- Glen Helen Regional Park: campground 'closed until further notice'.
- Mission RV Park, Redlands: park rules say 'No tent camping or sleeping outside of your RV'.
- San Bernardino RV Park: monthly stays only.
- Cherry Valley Lakes RV Resort: membership resort; non-members get in only through a sales-presentation stay.
- Kountry Manor Hipcamp, Loma Linda: RV-only, no toilets listed.
- Olive Dell Ranch, Colton: clothing-optional club; its website is now a parked domain, so status is unknown.
- Oak Glen Glamping: a wagon, not a tent site.
- Hoegees and Spruce Grove: hike-in only from Chantry Flat.
- Mt Lowe and Idlehour: closed.

Beyond the 10-mi limit (closer options exist):
- Prado Regional Park: 13.7 mi south. Designated tent spaces, hot showers; book online at least 24 h ahead; 909-465-5291.
- Lake Perris SRA hike-and-bike sites: $10, showers, 951-940-5603. 17–19.5 mi off with 1,300–1,750 ft of climbing.
- Chino Hills SP Rolling M Ranch: about 15 mi; not verified.
- Camp Williams, East Fork San Gabriel: $100 tent spots, 12+ mi up Hwy 39, no refunds.
- Glenn Camp: $5, bike-in on the West Fork bikeway, about 19 mi from Azusa. USFS pages disagree on whether it is open.
- Bonita Ranch and Applewhite, Lytle Creek: 10–13 mi with 1,800+ ft of climbing.
- Manker Flat: 6,000 ft, water off for the season.

Research note: the shared web-search limit was already used up when this step started, so no web searches were run. This list comes from OpenStreetMap, operator and agency websites, and The Dyrt, Campendium and Hipcamp pages fetched directly. Access distances come from the Valhalla bike router. Still to check by phone: Fairplex and Country Hills tent policies, and whether Gould Mesa is open. I found no churches or community sites that host cyclists, but I could not search for them.

camps.name: Vekol Valley Road BLM dispersed (Sonoran Desert National Monument)

BLM warns the southern monument is a smuggling corridor. No water anywhere: carry everything from Casa Grande or Stanfield.

camps.cyclistNotes: Legal and close to an interchange; Campendium rates it 5.0 across 22 reviews (latest Nov 2025: no one else there, no road noise). A reviewer felt 'very comfortable and safe'. camps.name: Painted Rock Petroglyph Campground (BLM)
camps.access: I-8 exit 102 (Painted Rock Dam Rd), then 10.7 mi north on paved road and 0.6 mi west on dirt Rocky Point Rd. Gentle grades. camps.name: BLM land on Agua Caliente Rd, north of Sentinel exit 87
camps.access: I-8 exit 87 (Sentinel), past Conde's and the Chevron, then north-west on paved Agua Caliente Rd. The first ~1.5 mi is State Trust land; BLM begins about 1.6 mi from I-8 (32.8804,-113.2259) and continues along the road. A BLM strip also lies about 0.4–1 mi south of I-8, behind a private frontage parcel, with no mapped road. Further east and south is the Goldwater Range: keep out.
camps.priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
camps.cyclistNotes: I found no camper reports for this exact spot. Land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, and BLM land is open to dispersed camping unless posted. Check for 'no camping' signs and camp out of sight of the road. Water and snacks at Conde's Middle of Nowhere and the Chevron at the exit (hours unverified). The State Trust land closer to I-8 is legal only with an Arizona State Land Department recreation permit.

research.waterAndFood:
Casa Grande is the last store directly on the line until Gila Bend. Near mile 0–1 there are QuikTrip and Fasttrip on N Pinal Ave, and 76/Good2Go plus Subway on W Gila Bend Hwy. From mile 1 to mile 59.3, nothing sits on I-8 itself.

Detours on the way to Gila Bend:
- Mammoth Homestead (mile 10.8): water for booked guests only.
- Stanfield (exit 161, mile 17.1), 3.5 mi north: Family Dollar (in OSM), plus Circle K and the El Rancho market and restaurant (per the West Pinal Park host, Nov 2024).
- Wild West RV Ranch store on AZ 84: snacks, drinks, beer and wine, potable water.
- Exit 151 (AZ 84, mile 27.2): OSM marks the station there as an abandoned building (checked May 2024). A Nov 2024 camp-host note mentions gas and showers there, but treat it as dry.
- Exits 144 (Vekol) and 140 (Freeman), West Pinal Park and every BLM site: no water.

Gila Bend:
- Pilot and Holt's Shell at exit 119 (mile 59.3).
- In town: Shell/One 9 (61.8), Gila Bend Food Market (62.6), Super K (63.0), Chevron (63.3), Circle K (63.4) and Love's (63.5), plus McDonald's, Sofia's Mexican food and fast food.
- Truck stops like Pilot and Love's usually sell showers to anyone, which helps if you camp on BLM land.

West of Gila Bend:
- Nothing from Love's (63.5) to Sentinel exit 87 (mile 92.2).
- Sentinel has Conde's Middle of Nowhere convenience store and a Chevron. Both are in OSM; hours unverified.
- Painted Rock campground has no water.
- After Sentinel, the next stop is the Dateland Travel Center (about mile 111).

Longest stretches with no water:
- Casa Grande to the Gila Bend Pilot: about 58 mi on I-8. That drops to about 42 mi if you refill in Stanfield, or about 37 mi from Wild West's store on the AZ 84 alternative.
- Gila Bend to Sentinel: 28.7 mi. It becomes about 48 mi to Dateland if Conde's is closed.

Leave Casa Grande or Stanfield and Gila Bend with 6+ litres, and add 4+ litres for any dry night on BLM land or at Painted Rock.
research.legality:
Bikes on I-8:
- From exit 174 (mile 4.3) to Sentinel, I-8 is a 75 mph rural interstate with two lanes each way and heavy trucks.
- Every I-8 piece I sampled in OpenStreetMap (5 points from Casa Grande to Sentinel) is tagged bicycle=yes. That fits ADOT allowing bikes on rural interstate shoulders unless signed otherwise. I found no 2026 construction notices, but web search was unavailable.
- Through Gila Bend the line leaves at exit 119, follows Butterfield Trail and Pima St (I-8 Business), and rejoins at exit 115.
- AZ 84 (the two-lane Gila Bend–Casa Grande Hwy) is a legal off-interstate alternative from Casa Grande via Stanfield to exit 151. It passes Wild West RV Ranch and West Pinal Park. Shoulder width is unverified.

Interchanges by corridor mile: 174 Trekell 4.3, 172 Thornton 5.6, 167 Montgomery 10.8, 161 Stanfield 17.1, 151 AZ 84 27.2, 144 Vekol 33.8, 140 Freeman 37.6–38.1, 119 Butterfield Trail 58.7, 115 Gila Bend/AZ 85 65.0, 111 Citrus Valley 68.2, 106 Paloma 73.2, 102 Painted Rock Dam Rd 77.0, 87 Sentinel 92.6. There is no exit between 140 and 119: 21 mi over the Maricopa Mountains.

Camping rules on BLM land:
- BLM says dispersed camping is allowed throughout the Sonoran Desert National Monument unless posted, with a 14-day limit.
- Bicycles are banned inside designated wilderness (North and South Maricopa Mountains, Table Top). On roads 8029 and 8030 the non-wilderness corridor is only about 50 ft each side of the road.
- BLM warns that the southern monument is a drug and human smuggling corridor. Border Patrol traffic is constant around Vekol.

Gated BLM roads with no ramp:
- 8029, 8030, 8032 and 8035 leave the westbound shoulder through gates. 8042 (MP 147.5) and 8011 leave the eastbound lanes and cannot be reached riding west.
- Arizona allows entering or leaving a controlled-access highway only at designated interchanges, so these gates are a gray-area emergency option.
- The legal ways in are Vekol (exit 144), Freeman (exit 140) and the Old Highway 84 dirt track from exit 119, which reaches the 8035 area.

Land status (from the BLM Surface Management Agency map):
- Gila Bend to about mile 79: private land on both sides.
- Miles 79.5–83.6: BLM on both sides, but there is no exit.
- South of I-8 from about mile 84 to Sentinel: Barry M. Goldwater Range (USAF), closed without a range permit.
- Painted Rock Dam Rd: Tohono O'odham (BIA) land from about 3 to 10 mi north of I-8.
- State Trust land at exit 119 and just north of exit 87: camping only with an Arizona State Land Department recreation permit.

Other rules found:
- Sonoran Desert RV Park's posted rules ban tents.
- The Gila Bend AFAF FamCamp is for DoD ID holders only.

Road surfaces:
- Vekol Rd: graded gravel with washboard.
- Freeman exit to W Old 84: old, unmaintained pavement, then rough gravel.
- Old Highway 84 east of exit 119: compacted dirt, rated 'bad' for smoothness in OSM.
- Painted Rock Dam Rd: 10.7 mi paved, then 0.6 mi dirt.
- Agua Caliente Rd at Sentinel: paved.
research.gapWarnings:
1) Gila Bend has no confirmed tent campground.
- Sonoran Desert RV Park is the app's current 'best bet' marked 'tents confirmed'. Its posted rules say tents are no longer allowed, even on RV sites, and it is 55+.
- Palms MH & RV Park and Augie's Quail Trail are unverified, and Augie's website no longer resolves.
- The Gila Bend AFAF FamCamp is military-ID only.
- Fallback: free BLM land along the Old Highway 84 dirt track, about 2 mi east of the Pilot at exit 119. Fill water at the Pilot or Love's first.

2) Miles ~57 to ~93 (about 36 mi) have no tent camp on the line. This runs from the Old Hwy 84 BLM land east of Gila Bend to the BLM land at Sentinel.
- The only fallback is Painted Rock Petroglyph Campground at exit 102 (mile 77.0). It is 11.3 mi north each way on paved road and has no water.
- If the Sentinel BLM land turns out to be posted or unsafe, the next tent sites are around Aztec in segment I8-B: Sun Portal Acres and Aztec Hills Retreat (Hipcamp, about mile 106–107, about 2.5 mi off) and Oasis RV Park at Aztec Hills (mile 109.2).
- That is about 50 mi past Gila Bend, with water only at Sentinel.

3) Casa Grande area, miles 0–22: no verified tent site directly on the line.
- Mammoth Homestead (Hipcamp, mile 10.8 plus about 2 mi) is the only one.
- Motoland is weekends only.
- Pinal County Fairgrounds is 11 mi back east.
- Casa Grande and Eloy RV resorts are 55+ and RV-only: Palm Creek, Sundance 1, Encore Fiesta Grande, Casita Verde, Foothills West, Silverado, Desert Springs and RoVer's Roost.
- The baseline 'Unnamed campground' on N Pinal Ave is unidentified.

4) Bad-wind days of 50 miles:
- From Casa Grande, the legal free camps reached from an interchange are Vekol (mile 33.8) and Freeman (mile 37.8–38.1).
- The next legal one is the Old Hwy 84 BLM land at Gila Bend, about 61 riding miles from Casa Grande.
- In between there are only the gray-area gate roads: 8029 at mile 42.1, 8030 at 48.2 and 8032 at 50.7.
- From Gila Bend, a short day ends at Painted Rock (about 25 riding miles) or Sentinel (about 30).

5) Distances for the decision:
- Casa Grande to Wild West RV Ranch (showers): about 26 riding miles via the Stanfield/AZ 84 loop.
- Casa Grande to West Pinal Park: about 28.
- Casa Grande to Gila Bend: about 59–61.
- Casa Grande to the Sentinel BLM land: about 94.
- Gila Bend to Sentinel: about 29.

result.advisories: As of ~9:30 PM MST Sun Nov 1: NO wind advisory, high wind warning or red flag warning anywhere on the three lines for Nov 2-8. ARIZONA (NWS Phoenix): Sunday's storm dropped 0.5-1.5 in. on the lower deserts; rivers and washes are running, some at flood stage. Flood Watch until 5 AM MST Mon covers West Pinal (Casa Grande/Maricopa), Buckeye/Avondale, Tonopah Desert and Gila Bend zones. Flood Warnings in effect tonight include the Hassayampa River (low-water crossings at Hassayampa/Arlington, to 3:45 AM Mon) and the New River (low-water crossings downstream to the Gila may become impassable; to 11:15 AM Mon). PSR expects flood warnings to be extended through Monday. For the Nov 2 ride: wet shoulders and possibly closed or flowing dips on AZ 238, Rainbow Valley Rd, Tuthill/Beloat Rds and Baseline Rd/Salome Hwy (Hassayampa, Centennial Wash) - check Maricopa County/ADOT closures (az511.gov) and never ride through moving water. Casa Grande tonight: showers/T-storms until ~2 AM (a few could be severe, damaging-wind threat), WSW gusts to 30 mph; Monday sunny, high ~69, W 0-5 mph; patchy fog possible Mon AM in sheltered valleys. Rest of week dry, highs a few degrees below normal, light winds with modest afternoon upslope gusts; late-week shortwave PoP <=10%. SAN DIEGO (NWS SGX): Beach Hazards Statement for San Diego and Orange County coasts through Mon afternoon (surf 3-6 ft, minor tidal overflow near the ~3:30 PM high tide). High tides rise to ~7 ft by Fri and ~7.5 ft over the weekend into early next week - possible overwash of beach-level paths/campsites on the I-8 coast segment. Pattern: weak N/NE offshore flow Mon; weak trough Tue (light drizzle chance coastal SD County, backing off; onshore breeze Tue afternoon); weak offshore Wed-Thu; ridge Fri-weekend warming coast and low deserts to the low/mid 80s; ~23% of ensemble members show a deeper late-week low with somewhat stronger offshore winds. LOS ANGELES (NWS LOX): Beach Hazards Statement for LA/Ventura beaches through Mon afternoon; Sunday's post-frontal W gusts of 30-40 mph on the coast are over. Weak offshore flow all week; offshore gradients increase late week and peak Sat Nov 7 near -4 mb, giving gusty offshore winds mainly in LA/Ventura County mountains and valleys; recent rain mitigates fire risk. Ridge holds to ~Nov 10; next rain-bearing trough ~Nov 11. No Santa Ana advisory has been issued; the NWS grids show this weak offshore event as NE 13-17 mph g22-26 at Jacumba/Pine Valley Nov 6-8, ENE/E 10-17 g16-26 at Banning Nov 5-8 (strongest at dawn), N 8-14 g17-25 down the lower Colorado River (Blythe/Yuma/Quartzsite) and Desert Center-Chiriaco Nov 6-8, and NNW 9-14 g16-23 at dawn Nov 6-7 on the Coachella Valley floor (Indio/Mecca).
result.climatology: Computed for this trip from station archives (IEM copies of NWS-ingested obs), November riding hours 8 AM-5 PM local; 'westerly' = from SW through NW (head or quartering-head wind for a westbound rider); RAWS anemometers at 20 ft, ASOS at 33 ft; 'brutal day' = mean headwind component >=15 mph or any hour >=25 mph. SAN GORGONIO PASS: (1) Whitewater RAWS (WWAC1, 2,530 ft, pass mouth beside the I-10/CA 111 wind farms the bike line crosses near mi 325-340; Nov 2011-2025): westerly >=15 mph in 28% of riding hours, >=20 in 23%, >=25 in 15%. When it blows it is strong: median 24 mph, 90th pct 33 mph sustained; westerly gusts median 36, 90th pct 49, max 75 mph. ~8.7 brutal days per November (29% of days), usually in 2-day spells (longest 7). It is bimodal: 41% of days net a light tailwind (SE up-valley breeze or E offshore flow, rarely >=15 mph) and 27% are light/variable. An onshore westerly blows all day once it sets in (25% of hours at 8 AM vs 31% at 3 PM), so an early start does not dodge it. (2) Cabazon (BAZC1, 2,150 ft, mid-pass on the bike line; Nov 2012-2025): westerly >=15 mph in 14% of hours, >=20 only 2%; median 13 / 90th pct 18 mph; gusts median 21, max 48. Easterly >=15 mph is more common here in November (27% of hours); ~2.5 brutal + ~8 moderate-headwind days per November, 51% of days net tailwind. Westerlies here peak midday (7% of hours at 7 AM vs 20% at noon), so early starts help on the Cabazon-Banning half. (3) Palm Springs airport (KPSP, valley floor; Nov 2010-2025): 74% of riding hours under 8 mph, westerly >=15 just 2%, essentially no brutal days - the wind is confined to the Whitewater-Cabazon corridor, not the city. Contrast May 2021-2025: Whitewater westerly >=15 mph in 67% of hours and 72% of days brutal; Cabazon 59% / 48%. November is the pass's gentle season, with roughly a third as many brutal days as late spring (consistent with AMS work showing California pass winds peak in the warm months). OCOTILLO / IN-KO-PAH (I-8): (1) Jacumba-Mountain Springs Grade (TNSC1, 2,140 ft, on I-8 above the Ocotillo wind farm; Nov 2014-2025): 61% of riding hours under 8 mph; SW-W >=15 mph in 14% of hours, >=20 in 6%, >=25 in 2%; median 16 / 90th pct 25 mph when westerly; gusts median 27, 90th pct 40, max 55. ~3.1 brutal days per November (10%) plus ~11% moderate-headwind days, spells 1-2 days. The strong wind is SW gap flow straight down the grade - a direct headwind on the westbound climb - and it builds in the afternoon (10-11% of morning hours vs 16% after noon), so climb in the morning. NE offshore tailwind ~8% of days. May contrast: >=15 mph in 25% of hours, 24% brutal days. (2) El Centro NAF (KNJK, Imperial Valley floor; Nov 2010-2025): 71% of riding hours light, westerly >=15 mph 8%, ~2.4 brutal days per November. BOTTOM LINE: in an average November the I-10 pass mouth carries about a 3-in-10 daily chance of a 20-35 mph headwind (gusts 35-50), versus about 1-in-10 for a brutal day on the I-8 grade - normally I-8 is the wind-safer line in November. This week's forecast removes the pass risk.
result.summary: VERDICT: the coming week favors the I-10 corridor. All three lines get an unusually benign, dry week after Sunday's storm - no wind advisories, and the strongest forecast headwinds a westbound rider would meet are 10-14 mph (coastal afternoon sea breezes Nov 3 and 6, a 7-8 AM WSW 12 gap wind at Ocotillo Nov 4, and a dawn down-valley NNW 9-14 g16-23 at Indio/Mecca Nov 6-7). Why I-10: (1) shortest - 440 mi vs 486 Hybrid and 514 I-8; (2) its signature risk, the San Gorgonio Pass (~mi 320-351), which in an average November throws a 20-35 mph westerly on about 3 days in 10, is forecast to run EASTERLY (a tailwind up the climb) every day Thu Nov 5 - Sun Nov 8 (Banning ENE/E 10-17 mph at dawn, gusts 16-26, easing to 5-10 by midday), with Wed Nov 4 light/variable; only Tue Nov 3 shows an onshore WSW 8 g15 afternoon there, before he can arrive; (3) at any pace from 70 to 100 mi/day he reaches the pass Nov 5-6, and even a 1-2 day slip lands on Nov 7-8, the strongest tailwind days. SUGGESTED I-10 TIMING (~85 mi/day): Mon 11/2 Casa Grande -> Buckeye or Tonopah (calm, highs ~70; post-flood caution at washes/low-water crossings). Tue 11/3 Tonopah -> Quartzsite (calm; the Salome Hwy/US 60 variant is equally calm, so pick it on shoulder, traffic and services, not wind). Wed 11/4 Quartzsite -> Blythe -> Desert Center or Chiriaco (N crosswind 5-9 mph, gusts to 20 near Blythe at midday). Thu 11/5 -> Indio -> Palm Springs -> Cabazon/Banning (light winds everywhere; light ENE tailwind up the pass). Fri 11/6 Banning -> Redlands -> Claremont -> Pasadena -> Elysian (~95 mi; E tailwind at the top, calm west of Redlands) or split Fri/Sat. I-10 WATCH-OUTS: N crosswinds 8-14 mph g17-25 on the lower Colorado River and Desert Center-Chiriaco Nov 6-8; the dawn NNW wind at Indio/Mecca Nov 6-7 is a quartering headwind on the WNW leg to Palm Springs (start that leg after ~10 AM); warmest days Nov 7-8 (mid-80s in the Coachella Valley). The Box Canyon variant (Nov 5-7) would put the N wind behind him on the SW-bound descent but adds 12 mi plus a NW-bound leg into that same dawn wind. I-8: also wind-friendly (calm Arizona Nov 2-5; NE offshore tailwind on the In-Ko-Pah climb and through Jacumba-Pine Valley-Alpine Nov 5-8, with gusts 22-26 on exposed grades Nov 6-8; coast light N mornings and WNW 8-10 mph sea-breeze afternoons, a mild headwind northbound). But it costs +74 mi, a ~4,000-ft climb and colder mountain camps (Jacumba/Pine Valley lows 45-52F vs 49-65F along the I-10 line; the Salome variant also dips to 44-48F). In a normal November the I-8 grade is the wind-safer choice (brutal days ~1 in 10 vs ~3 in 10 at Whitewater); this week that advantage disappears. HYBRID: +46 mi over I-10 with the same pass timing (Nov 5-7), but CA 111 and CV Link run NW into the Nov 6-7 dawn NNW wind near Mecca/Indio; no wind reason to choose it this week. CONFIDENCE: high Nov 2-5, moderate Nov 6-8 (SGX ensembles split on a late-week low; ~23% show stronger offshore winds, which would still be tail/crosswinds westbound). Re-pull the Banning/Palm Springs forecast the evening before the pass day - an onshore surge would show as W/WSW >=15 mph in those grids.
